providers.name: Strategic Blue
providers.description: Strategic Blue is a UK-headquartered cloud FinOps company founded in 2010 by Dr James Mitchell, a former commodities trader. It specialises in AWS rate optimization through commitment management, delivering Reserved Instance and Savings Plan savings of up to 40-45% without lock-in, forecasting burden, or technical compromise. Strategic Blue treats cloud like a commodity, applying price-risk-management techniques from financial markets to optimize AWS discounts. Its Automate service serves commercial enterprises while Accelerate serves the UK public sector. The company operates on a least-privilege model, accessing only cost and usage metadata and never customer cloud environments. It is ISO 27001, ISO 9001, and ISO 14001 certified, CSA STAR and Cyber Essentials registered, and an AWS Advanced and Google Cloud Premier partner.

providers.name: Heriot-Watt University
providers.description: Heriot-Watt University is a public research university based in Edinburgh, Scotland, with additional campuses in the Scottish Borders, Orkney, Dubai, and Malaysia. It is ranked #257 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Heriot-Watt's public, machine-readable footprint centers on its Research Portal (powered by Elsevier Pure) for research outputs, projects, and expertise, and on Ex Libris Alma/Primo library Discovery and Springshare LibCal services. The university does not operate a public developer portal; programmatic interfaces such as the Pure OAI-PMH/REST API and the LibCal API exist as platform features but are gated and require credentials or institutional arrangement rather than being openly self-service.

providers.name: BT Group
providers.description: BT Group plc (British Telecommunications) is the United Kingdom's largest fixed-line, broadband, and mobile communications provider, headquartered in London with operations spanning consumer, business, wholesale, and global enterprise markets. The group is organised around three customer-facing brands — BT, EE, and Plusnet — and a wholesale division that sells capacity and access to other communications providers. BT Group operates the UK's largest mobile network (EE), runs fibre and copper access through Openreach (a legally separate group company), and provides networked IT and security services to multinational enterprises and the UK public sector. The group publishes a public developer programme at developer.bt.com that exposes a growing catalogue of REST APIs across two main domains: charging and crediting (Direct Carrier Billing, Crediting, Premium SMS) and digital identity / fraud prevention (SIM Swap, Network Identity, Call Divert Protection), alongside wholesale and operational APIs (Broadband One, Quote Management, Address Management, Appointment Management, Product and Network Availability, HubCo Voice, Global Voice Services, IMEI Lookup, Home Network, Rail Insights, Location Insights for London, and a Travel Journey API Platform). The portal supports sandbox onboarding with Client ID / Client Secret OAuth 2.0 credentials and progression to production under a commercial agreement with an account team. In April 2025 BT announced a federated API management partnership with Kong (Kong Konnect) to consolidate its previously fragmented API estate, strengthen governance, and offer a self-service developer experience across the group.

providers.name: REalyse
providers.description: REalyse is a UK residential property data platform that aggregates more than 100 data sources into geospatial analysis and market-intelligence tools for developers, lenders, investors, consultants, and funds. Its data spans five domains — Planning & Policy, Demographics, Market (rental and sales pricing, yields, days on market, comparables), Land & Ownership, and Amenities. REalyse offers a data API for institutions that require a constant feed of property data, alongside the REalyse Core geospatial platform, the REalyse Pulse consumer AI valuation product, and downloadable Market Intelligence reports. The company is based in London and is backed by Anthemis. API access is onboarded through the sales team rather than a self-service developer portal, so no public OpenAPI, base URL, or authentication reference is published.

providers.name: Propertymark
providers.description: Propertymark is the United Kingdom's largest professional body for property agents, formed in 2017 from the merger of the National Association of Estate Agents (NAEA), the Association of Residential Letting Agents (ARLA), the Institute of Commercial and Business Agents (ICBA) and the National Association of Valuers and Auctioneers (NAVA), and representing "over 19,000 members" across residential sales, lettings, commercial property, inventories, auctions and valuation. Its home market is the United Kingdom - England, Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland and the Channel Islands. In the property value chain it sits on the agent-accreditation and consumer-protection side, not the listings side: it publishes the Conduct and Membership Rules, operates a government-approved Client Money Protection scheme, runs Propertymark Qualifications as the sector's specialist awarding organisation, and lobbies government on estate and letting agency regulation. Its API posture is the flat, honest zero. There is no developer portal, no documented API, no SDK, no webhooks and no published machine-readable contract of any kind: developer.propertymark.co.uk, developers.propertymark.co.uk, api.propertymark.co.uk, data.propertymark.co.uk and standards.propertymark.co.uk all fail DNS resolution, and /openapi.json, /swagger.json, /api-docs, /api, /developers, /docs, /$metadata and /odata all return honest HTTP 404s from www.propertymark.co.uk. RESO is entirely absent - the site's own search returns "result: 0 of 0" for both "RESO" and "OData" - because the United Kingdom has no MLS and therefore no listing-data certification layer to be certified against; UK residential listings reach consumers through the Rightmove/Zoopla portal duopoly via agency CRM software, several of whose vendors (Reapit, Street, MRI Software, Dezrez, AgentOS, Coadjute, and Rightmove itself) appear in Propertymark's own Industry Supplier directory. What Propertymark does publish freely is its rulebook: the Propertymark Conduct and Membership Rules PDF downloads anonymously with no login and no EULA. Its only machine-readable surface is undocumented - an internal Preside CMS JSON endpoint behind the public Find an Expert member directory - and its member area is SAML-gated, returning HTTP 401. Genuinely open UK property data comes from HM Land Registry and Ordnance Survey, not from the agents' professional body.

providers.name: Queen Mary University of London
providers.description: Queen Mary University of London (QMUL) is a public research university in London, United Kingdom, and a member of the Russell Group, ranked #120 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public, machine-accessible footprint is research- and library-oriented rather than a formal developer program: Queen Mary Research Online (QMRO) is an open-access DSpace institutional repository that exposes a standards-based OAI-PMH metadata-harvesting interface, and the university maintains a public GitHub organization (QMUL) for code released by its staff. QMUL does not publish a central, branded developer portal with signup-gated REST APIs; core student, timetable, and library platforms (QMplus/Moodle, MyQMUL, library discovery) sit behind institutional authentication.

providers.name: Redwood Bank
providers.description: Redwood Bank is a specialist UK challenger bank for small and medium-sized businesses, headquartered in Letchworth Garden City, Hertfordshire. Launched in 2017 after receiving its banking licence from the Prudential Regulation Authority and Financial Conduct Authority (Financial Services Register firm reference 755924, company number 09872265), it is wholly owned by Redwood Financial Partners Ltd — a vehicle controlled by Jonathan and David Rowland, with Warrington Borough Council holding a roughly one-third stake. Redwood focuses narrowly on business and charity savings accounts and individually underwritten commercial and buy-to-let mortgages, and is not one of the CMA9 mandated banks. Because its product range is deposit- and lending-only (it does not offer a payment / business current account), it falls outside the PSD2 scope that compels UK Open Banking, and as of this review it publishes no public developer portal, no OBIE Read/Write (AIS/PIS/CBPII) APIs, and no confirmed Open Banking Open Data endpoint.

providers.name: Urban Jungle
providers.description: Urban Jungle Services Ltd is a London-based direct-to-consumer insurtech, founded in 2016 by Jimmy Williams and Greg Smyth to sell home insurance to "Generation Rent" — renters, sharers and students the traditional UK market underserves. It is an FCA-authorised intermediary (FRN 782061, company number 10414152, England and Wales) and a certified B Corp, selling contents, buildings and contents, students contents, tenants liability, landlord, home emergency and public liability cover through its own digital journey at myurbanjungle.com, and claiming over 100,000 customers. Its API posture is partner-gated and undocumented in public. Urban Jungle announced a partnership programme and quote API in 2018, positioned so lettings agents, PropTech firms, institutional landlords and eCommerce sites can serve Urban Jungle quotes inside their own apps without being directly FCA-regulated themselves, but there is no developer portal, no reference documentation, no machine- readable specification and no self-serve signup. The only route in is a partnerships email address on a marketing page. No ACORD, AL3 or NGDS reference appears anywhere on the company's site or in its front-end bundles.

providers.name: Lawhive
providers.description: Lawhive is a UK consumer legal-services marketplace that connects individuals and small businesses with regulated solicitors online at fixed, transparent prices, positioned as roughly half the cost of a traditional high-street law firm. Clients answer intake questions on the site, receive a quote or a callback, and are matched with a vetted consultant lawyer who then runs the matter end to end through the Lawhive platform, covering conveyancing, divorce and family, employment, immigration, landlord and tenant, and property work. Lawhive Ltd is not a law firm and does not give legal advice itself; regulated legal services are delivered by its network, including affiliate firm Lawhive Legal Ltd, which is authorised and regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA ID 8003766). The company is backed by Balderton Capital and GV. Lawhive publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation, so this profile captures its identity, legal and compliance posture, and probed domain-security surface rather than an API contract.

providers.name: Investly
providers.description: Investly is a European fintech invoice-financing marketplace that helps growing small and medium-sized businesses unlock working capital by financing their outstanding 30-180 day invoices. Businesses sell their approved invoices through a reverse-auction marketplace where investors bid to fund them, giving merchants the best available price from multiple funding providers and access to cash in 1-3 working days rather than waiting on customer payment terms. Founded by Siim Maivel and operating across Estonia and the United Kingdom, Investly is backed by Speedinvest, Startup Wise Guys, and Founders Capital. The platform serves established businesses across manufacturing, wholesale, construction, logistics, and business-services sectors and has funded invoices worth tens of millions of pounds to date. Investly runs a production HAL/HATEOAS backend API at api.investly.co, though it does not currently publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or API reference documentation.

providers.name: MORI
providers.description: MORI (Baby Mori) is a UK-based, online-first baby and children's brand founded in 2015 by Akin Onal, known for soft essentials made from a proprietary bamboo and organic cotton fabric blend. Its direct-to-consumer range spans sleepwear, daywear, footwear, blankets and muslins, nursery and home goods, and a Sleep Club subscription, shipping across the UK, US, and Europe. MORI operates as a Shopify-hosted e-commerce business and does not publish a first-party developer API. Its machine-readable surface is provided natively by the Shopify platform: a live Storefront MCP server at /api/mcp (search_catalog, get_cart, update_cart, get_product_details, search_shop_policies_and_faqs), a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile at /.well-known/ucp, an agent-instructions /llms.txt (mirrored at /agents.md), and the Shopify Customer Account API OIDC/OAuth discovery. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Accurx
providers.description: Accurx is a United Kingdom clinical communication and workflow company, founded in 2016 and headquartered in London, whose software is used across NHS primary care, secondary care, and community and mental health services to message patients, run patient triage, batch-message cohorts, book and remind appointments, and (via its Scribe product) draft clinical notes with AI. Accurx integrates around the NHS as an assured IM1 live supplier, using NHS Digital's interoperability standards for primary care and connecting bi-directionally to the GP clinical-system duopoly (EMIS Health, TPP SystmOne) and Vision, plus NHS national services including the Personal Demographics Service (PDS), NHS Single Sign-On, NHS Login, and the NHS App. Accurx is a consumer and integrator of NHS FHIR and IM1 interfaces rather than a publisher of its own public developer API: as of this review it operates no public developer portal, no self-serve REST/FHIR API, and no downloadable OpenAPI or FHIR CapabilityStatement. Third-party and trust integrations are arranged through its partnerships and integration teams under partner agreement.

providers.name: ANNA Money
providers.description: ANNA Money (a trading name of Absolutely No Nonsense Admin Ltd, company number 10149389, Cardiff, a subsidiary of ANNA Holdings Ltd) is a UK digital business account and tax app for freelancers, startups, and small businesses, positioned as a challenger to the high-street banks. ANNA is not a bank but an e-money proposition: its Mastercard and e-money services are issued by PayrNet Limited, authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority for electronic money service activities (FCA FRN 900594), and its Account Information Services are provided under agency of TrueLayer (FCA FRN 901096). Within UK Open Banking, ANNA is a consumer / third-party provider (TPP) rather than an account-holding ASPSP or a CMA9 mandated bank - it uses TrueLayer's Data and Payments APIs for external account aggregation, automatic VAT calculation, and QR-code "pay by bank" collection. ANNA publishes no public developer portal, no Open Data API, and no OBIE Read/Write (AIS/PIS/CBPII) API surface of its own; its public GitHub organisation hosts open-source engineering tooling (asyncio, aiohttp, and Postgres libraries) rather than product APIs.

providers.name: Bippit
providers.description: Bippit is a UK-based financial wellbeing platform that gives every employee access to personal, qualified financial coaching alongside AI-powered guidance available 24/7, planning and budgeting tools, payroll savings, and educational content and webinars. Sold to employers as a workplace benefit, it also provides organisations with aggregate financial-wellbeing insights and analytics. Bippit is FCA-regulated (No. 845814), ICO-registered (No. ZA533579), ISO 27001:2022 certified, and GDPR / UK DPA 2018 compliant, with data stored in the EEA. Backed by Techstars. Bippit publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web and compliance surface.

providers.name: OnTheMarket
providers.description: OnTheMarket is the third-largest residential property portal in the United Kingdom, operating onthemarket.com. It was founded in 2013 by Agents' Mutual Limited as an agent-owned challenger to Rightmove and Zoopla, listed on AIM as OnTheMarket plc, and was acquired outright by CoStar Group in December 2023 for approximately GBP 99 million. In a market with no MLS and no cooperative listing standard, OnTheMarket sits at the demand end of the value chain: consumers search the portal, and listings arrive from member estate agents' CRM systems rather than from a shared data pool. Its API posture is honest and narrow. There is no public developer portal — developer., developers., api. and docs.onthemarket.com do not resolve, and /developers, /api, /docs, /openapi.json, /swagger.json and /api-docs all return 404 on the main site. What does exist is a member-only integration surface: the OnTheMarket Real Time Datafeed (RTDF), a Rightmove-RTDF-compatible feed API served from the live, OnTheMarket-operated host realtime-api.onthemarket.com, used by agency CRM vendors to push listings and pull branch enquiries on behalf of member agents. No machine-readable contract for it is published anywhere; OnTheMarket's developer guide is distributed under agreement, and every path on the host returns 404 to an anonymous caller. There is no RESO Web API or Data Dictionary certification, no OData $metadata document and no Universal Property Identifier anywhere in the stack — RESO is a North American construct and the UK has never adopted it, so "certified but unreachable" does not apply here; there is no certification layer in this market at all. OnTheMarket publishes no open data. The genuinely open UK property layer belongs to the public sector — HM Land Registry Price Paid Data and Ordnance Survey — and none of it comes from the portals. OnTheMarket's own Terms of Use go further than most and expressly forbid automated access to any page other than the home page.

providers.name: Convex
providers.description: Convex Group Limited is an international specialty insurer and reinsurer founded in 2019 by Stephen Catlin and Paul Brand, headquartered in London with operations in Bermuda, Luxembourg, Guernsey and the United States. Convex writes complex commercial and specialty risk across property, casualty, marine, energy, aviation, cyber, political risk and credit, crisis management, accident and health, and equine/livestock/aquaculture, and writes property, casualty and specialty treaty reinsurance through Convex Re Limited in Bermuda and London. Convex Insurance UK Limited is authorised by the Prudential Regulation Authority and regulated by the FCA and PRA; it is a London company-market carrier rather than a Lloyd's syndicate, and it reported roughly $5.2bn of gross written premium in 2024. Convex operates a named Digital Underwriting function that publicly describes building "a suite of insurance specific APIs" for automated quote and bind on high-volume, low-complexity specialty books, delivered either through a Convex-hosted broker portal or by connecting Convex products into a broker's or client's existing portal via API. That API programme is real but entirely partner-gated: as of 2026-07-25 Convex publishes no public developer portal, no API reference, no OpenAPI or other machine- readable definition, no sandbox and no self-serve signup. The api.convexin.com host is live but answers every anonymous request with HTTP 401 Unauthorized, the digital.convexin.com broker application is an authenticated Unqork-hosted portal, and the Convex Quick Quote event-insurance surface is behind a broker account registration form. Integration is arranged through the Business Development team, not through documentation. No ACORD, AL3, NGDS or IVANS reference appears anywhere on Convex's public web presence.

providers.name: Ultromics
providers.description: Ultromics is a UK-based clinical AI company, spun out of the University of Oxford and backed by GV, whose EchoGo platform applies FDA 510(k)-cleared AI to routine echocardiograms to help clinicians detect heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and cardiac amyloidosis. EchoGo integrates into existing hospital echo workflows and PACS environments, delivering results through clinical systems rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: Prudential plc
providers.description: Prudential plc is a life and health insurance and asset management group incorporated in England and Wales and listed on the London, Hong Kong, Singapore and New York exchanges, with its principal operating office in Hong Kong and roots in London going back to 1848. Its home market for this profile is the United Kingdom, but its book is almost entirely Asian and African: life protection, health and medical, savings and retirement, takaful, pensions and Hong Kong Mandatory Provident Funds, plus asset management under the Eastspring brand, across Hong Kong, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, Taiwan, India, mainland China, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar and a dozen African markets including Kenya, Uganda, Ghana, Nigeria and Zambia. It is no longer a UK retail insurer at all - the UK and Europe business was demerged as M&G plc in 2019 and the US business as Jackson Financial in 2021 - so the familiar UK "Pru" brands at pru.co.uk belong to M&G, not to this company. Its API posture is that there is no public API posture. Prudential plc publishes no developer portal, no API reference, no downloadable OpenAPI or Swagger document and no partner integration surface of any kind: developer, developers, docs, api, apis, partners, portal and sandbox subdomains of prudentialplc.com all fail to resolve, and /developers, /api, /developer, /partners and /integrations on the corporate site all return HTTP 404. The group's stated technology strategy is inward-facing - AI, automation, cloud and a global AI Lab running over a hundred internal use cases - and its distribution is built on tied agency forces and exclusive bancassurance partnerships with banks such as Standard Chartered, CIMB, MSB, SeABank, Bank Syariah Indonesia and UOB, which are commercial and contractual relationships rather than published API programmes. The Pulse by Prudential health and wealth app onboards health-tech and wealth-tech partners (Babylon, Tictrac, Halodoc, Smarter Health, Prive Technologies, OVO, Google Cloud) but every announcement describes the arrangement in commercial terms and none exposes a developer programme, SDK or public API. No ACORD, AL3, ACORD XML or NGDS reference was found anywhere in Prudential plc's public estate. Recorded honestly as a large carrier with a fully partner-gated, non-public integration surface. One genuine machine-readable surface does exist, and it is not an API: six of the group's market operating companies - Prudential Hong Kong, Prudential Singapore, Prudential Indonesia, Prudential Vietnam, Pru Life UK in the Philippines and Prudential BSN Takaful in Malaysia - publish real first-party llms.txt documents for grounding large language models, with Prudential Vietnam declaring a per-user-agent bot access policy for gptbot, claudebot, google-extended, perplexitybot and six other crawlers. The corporate domain publishes none. Underneath that, the group runs a visibly centralised security posture: TLS 1.3 and HSTS on every market host, and one shared PowerDMARC/PowerSPF tenant with a common aggregate-report mailbox across all seven domains, at p=reject on the corporate domain and p=quarantine in the markets, with no CAA record anywhere.

providers.name: Bloom & Wild
providers.description: Bloom & Wild is a British direct-to-consumer online florist and gifting brand founded in 2013 by Aron Gelbard and Ben Stanway, best known for pioneering letterbox flowers — bouquets packed flat so they fit through a UK letterbox — alongside hand-tied bouquets, plants, gift sets, gift cards and recurring flower subscriptions. Bloom & Wild Group trades as Bloom & Wild in the United Kingdom, Ireland, Germany and Austria, and operates the sister brands bloomon (Netherlands, Belgium, Denmark) and Bergamotte (France) on separate storefronts. The group is a certified B Corp and runs its own commerce platform — a Ruby on Rails backend fronted by Kong, an Angular multi-brand web app and native iOS and Android clients, on AWS and GCP. Bloom & Wild publishes NO public developer portal, no API documentation, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable API description, and no partner or corporate-gifting API: business and bulk gifting is transacted through a contact form, an account manager and invoicing, not through a programmatic surface. The application backends at api.bloomandwild.com and capi.bloomandwild.com are live but private to the brand's own clients and undocumented. What the group does publish for machines is narrow but real: an llms.txt on the UK and German storefronts that routes assistants to the correct market by delivery destination and even ships an optional agent widget specification, and an RFC 9116 security.txt served across every group storefront.

providers.name: Click Mechanic
providers.description: ClickMechanic is the UK's leading online car-repair marketplace, founded in 2012, that connects car owners with vetted mobile mechanics and independent garages for repairs, servicing, diagnostics, and MOTs. Customers enter their registration and symptoms to get an instant fixed-price quote, then book a vetted mechanic for same- or next-day work at home or the roadside, with payment taken only after the job is completed. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. ClickMechanic operates a consumer- and mechanic-facing web platform (Ruby on Rails on Heroku) and publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable API catalog at this time; this profile captures its public identity and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Satago
providers.description: Satago is a UK financial-technology platform offering a three-in-one cash flow management solution for small and medium-sized businesses: Risk Insights (real-time credit checks, risk bands, and suggested credit limits), Credit Control (automated invoice chasing with customizable email and SMS reminder sequences, statements, and late-fee handling), and Invoice Finance (fast, flexible funding with advance rates up to 90% on single or multiple invoices, offered as both selective and full facilities). The platform synchronizes with 300+ accounting packages including Sage, Xero, QuickBooks, KashFlow, and FreeAgent to keep debtor data current. Satago sells to businesses directly and through partners; it does not currently publish a public developer API, consuming the accounting platforms' APIs rather than exposing its own.

providers.name: Butternut Box
providers.description: Butternut Box is a London-headquartered direct-to-consumer pet nutrition company that cooks and delivers fresh, gently-steamed dog food on a personalised subscription. Customers complete an online profiling wizard covering their dog's breed, age, weight, activity level and health needs, and Butternut Box calculates a portioned meal plan from human-quality meat and vegetables, batch-cooks it at low temperature, freezes it, and ships it on a recurring schedule. Founded in 2016 and certified as a B Corporation, the company operates nine locale storefronts covering the United Kingdom, Ireland, the Netherlands, Belgium (Dutch and French), Germany, Italy, Sweden and Denmark, and runs its own production facility alongside a React / React Native / Ruby on Rails engineering stack. Butternut Box publishes no public developer API, developer portal or machine-readable specification; its customer-facing surfaces are the marketing site, the subscription web app and the iOS/Android apps.

providers.name: Direct Line Group
providers.description: Direct Line Group is a United Kingdom personal-lines and small-commercial general insurance carrier, founded in 1985 as the UK's first telephone-only motor insurer and listed on the London Stock Exchange from its 2012 IPO until Aviva plc completed its GBP 3.7 billion acquisition of the group on 1 July 2025. The group underwrites motor, home, pet, travel, landlord, breakdown and small-business insurance through the Direct Line, Churchill, Privilege, Darwin, By Miles, Direct Line for Business and Green Flag brands, and is regulated in its home market by the Financial Conduct Authority and the Prudential Regulation Authority. Its distribution is direct-to-consumer via telephone and web plus price-comparison-website placement (notably through the Darwin brand), rather than through broker or agency channels; it sold its brokered commercial business (NIG and FarmWeb) to RSA in September 2023, closing the one channel that would have carried standards-based broker integration. Its API posture is accordingly closed and partner-gated: as of 25 July 2026 the corporate domain directlinegroup.co.uk returns HTTP 301 to aviva.com, there is no developer.*, developers.* or docs.* host in DNS, every consumer brand site returns 404 on /developers, /api and /partners, and the only API host that exists — api.directlinegroup.co.uk, resolving to a MuleSoft Anypoint production load balancer — serves HTTP 403 behind an expired TLS certificate and requests a client certificate during the TLS handshake. There is no public self-serve developer portal, no downloadable OpenAPI, no GraphQL, no published webhook or event catalog, no public Postman workspace, and no ACORD reference anywhere in the group's public material. Quote, bind, issue and FNOL are all consumer web and telephone journeys only.

providers.name: HomeTouch
providers.description: HomeTouch (myhometouch.com) is a UK-based live-in home care marketplace founded in 2015 by Dr Jamie Wilson, a former NHS dementia specialist. The CQC-regulated service connects families with vetted professional carers for live-in, overnight, and visiting care, with a specialism in dementia and complex-needs support, hospital discharge, end-of-life, respite, and companionship care. Backed by 500 Global and other impact investors, HomeTouch operates a carer marketplace alongside a fully managed care service. The company publishes no public developer program or API; this profile tracks its identity, published web properties, and domain security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Spill
providers.description: Spill is a UK-based employee assistance programme (EAP) that delivers mental health support to employees directly inside the tools teams already use, such as Slack and Microsoft Teams. The platform offers same-day, message-based counselling, structured multi-session therapy courses for specific mental health conditions, drop-in group sessions, manager mental-health training, and self-guided wellbeing content, all through a single subscription. Spill serves over 600 companies on month-to-month terms and is backed by Seedcamp. It is a B2B software-as-a-service wellbeing product rather than an API provider; no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK has been published.

providers.name: Lendable
providers.description: Lendable Ltd is a UK consumer lending fintech founded in 2014 and headquartered in London, offering unsecured personal loans directly to borrowers through a fully digital application. The company underwrites with technology and data analytics rather than relying on a credit score alone, describing its approach as looking at all of an applicant's data together to produce a personalised quote in minutes without paper forms or branch visits. Lendable distributes through the major UK price-comparison platforms including ClearScore, Compare the Market, MoneySuperMarket, Experian, TotallyMoney, TransUnion and Go.Compare. It is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA reference 720261, company number 08828186) and is a CIFAS member. Lendable publishes no public developer API or developer portal — its public technical surface is an RFC 9116 security.txt, an llms.txt, and a set of first-party open source PHP/Symfony engineering libraries on Packagist and GitHub.

providers.name: Tem
providers.description: Tem (Tem-Energy Limited) is a UK-based energy technology company building AI-native transaction infrastructure for a modern energy market. Its RED platform is a modern utility that removes wholesale market markups to cut business electricity costs by up to 30%, provides transparent line-by-line billing from half-hourly meter data, and gives generators fairer earnings with renewable-energy traceability across 6,000+ sites. Backed by a February 2026 GBP 55M Series B led by Lightspeed Venture Partners. The customer-facing platform runs at app.tem.energy behind an OIDC login; the platform API at api.tem.energy is a private AWS API Gateway with no publicly documented developer surface at the time of profiling.

providers.name: Atom Learning
providers.description: Atom Learning is a UK edtech company providing an online, adaptive exam-preparation and learning platform for children aged 7 to 16. Its consumer product, Atom Home, delivers personalised practice, unlimited mock tests with instant marking, and progress tracking for 11+ grammar and independent-school entrance exams (GL, CEM, CSSE, ISEB), CAT4, Key Stage 2 SATs, and GCSE revision. Its schools product, Atom School, gives teachers curriculum-mapped resources and assessment tools and is used by over 1,000 schools. Founded by educators and assessment specialists, Atom has supported hundreds of thousands of families as a lower-cost alternative to private tutoring. The company was surfaced as a SoftBank Vision Fund portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes a consumer web/app product surface but no public developer API.

providers.name: BorrowMyDoggy
providers.description: BorrowMyDoggy is a UK-based platform that connects dog owners with trusted local borrowers for dog walking, sitting, boarding, and holiday care. Owners who cannot always be with their dog are matched with nearby dog lovers who want to spend time with a dog without the full-time commitment, so dogs get more walks, company, and care. Membership is free to join, with optional Premium tiers for owners and borrowers that unlock messaging, insurance cover, and a 24/7 vet line. The company operates a consumer web and mobile application built on Ruby on Rails; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched from public web surfaces.

providers.name: Immigram LTD
providers.description: Immigram is a UK relocation and immigration platform that helps IT specialists, engineers, founders, and entrepreneurs move to the United Kingdom, primarily via the Global Talent Visa (Tech Nation endorsement route) as well as Skilled Worker, settlement (ILR/naturalization), family, US O-1, and Spanish Startup visa paths. The company pairs immigration legal expertise with an AI-assisted platform that scores eligibility in advance, collects and reviews applicant data into a case, and tracks the process through a live dashboard with data-driven guidance and support. Founded in 2019 and backed by the 500 Global accelerator, Immigram is a services/SaaS provider and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Visibly
providers.description: Visibly is a UK-based workforce compliance management platform that helps enterprises with large, distributed and subcontracted workforces automate their HSEQ (health, safety, environment and quality) obligations. It centralizes worker onboarding, competency and certification tracking, real-time compliance monitoring and alerts, audit and project reporting, and safety broadcast communications, with integrations into existing HR, ERP, LMS and SharePoint systems and mobile-first workflows for field workers. It is used across construction, manufacturing, FMCG, energy, public services, infrastructure and logistics by organizations including Network Rail, National Grid, EDF, Scottish Power, NHS and Danone. Backed by Creandum and Seedcamp.

providers.name: Lantum
providers.description: Lantum (formerly Network Locum, founded 2012 in Shoreditch, London) is a United Kingdom healthcare workforce-management company whose Connected Scheduling platform helps NHS primary- and secondary-care organisations build digital staff banks, manage rotas and e-rostering, run automated timesheets and payments, and fill clinical shifts from a verified network of 30,000+ locum clinicians. It serves over 2,000 primary-care organisations, GP practices, PCNs, GP federations, and integrated care systems across the UK. Lantum is a practice-management and workforce platform rather than a clinical-data interoperability vendor, and it does NOT publish a public developer portal, a documented REST API, or an HL7 FHIR CapabilityStatement. Its product is delivered through a gated web and mobile application (lantum.com), onboarded via sales and demo request, with any system integrations (for example to GP clinical systems) handled through private partner arrangements rather than a self-serve public API.

providers.name: Serve First
providers.description: Serve First is a UK-based AI-driven customer experience (CX) platform that unifies reviews, surveys, receipts, in-location feedback terminals, operational audits, and mystery shopping into a single dashboard. It turns real-time customer feedback into role-based, actionable insight, with sentiment analysis and unified reporting across retail, hospitality, facilities management, health & wellness, and franchise businesses. Serve First also provides Client Connect journey/workflow automation and Martyn's Law public-protection compliance management. Serve First does not currently publish a public developer API or OpenAPI specification; this profile captures company identity plus verified security and compliance posture (SOC 2 and ISO 27001 via a Sprinto-hosted trust center).

providers.name: KareInn
providers.description: KareInn is a UK-based digital care management and care-home planning software provider whose cloud platform helps residential and nursing care providers streamline operations, evidence CQC compliance, and improve resident care. The product suite spans a care-management dashboard with occupancy and management reporting, a customizable care-plan builder, clinical policy and procedure workflows, care-delivery task assignment and monitoring, pre-admissions and occupancy pipeline management, event and incident tracking, and a resident and family engagement portal. KareInn integrates with partner systems including Civica/Coldharbour income processing, Camscope electronic medication management, and Ally Cares acoustic monitoring, and is positioned as an NHS assured supplier. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a Seedcamp portfolio lead; KareInn does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or a machine-readable discovery surface — the artifacts below capture its public product, commercial, and policy pages only.

providers.name: Wayhome
providers.description: Wayhome (formerly Unmortgage) is a London-based property technology company founded in 2016 by Nigel Purves and Josef Wasinski. It offers "Gradual Homeownership" — a part-buy, part-rent alternative to a traditional mortgage in which a customer buys at least 5% of a home and pays rent on the remainder, gradually increasing their ownership stake over time. Wayhome pairs aspiring homeowners with institutional investors (including Allianz), letting people who can afford rent but cannot secure a conventional mortgage move into a home of their choice with a deposit as low as 5%. Wayhome is authorised and regulated in the United Kingdom. It is backed by fintech venture investors including Anthemis, Augmentum Fintech, Allianz X and Accelerated Digital Ventures. Wayhome operates as a consumer-facing service and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public web, security, and domain-security surface.

providers.name: GetHarley
providers.description: GetHarley is a UK-based telehealth and skincare platform delivering personalised, medical-grade skincare through online consultations. Patients answer questions about their skin concerns, book a video consultation, and are matched with one of a network of over 1,000 licensed dermatologists, aesthetic doctors, and plastic surgeons, who recommend a tailored regimen of medical-grade products delivered to the patient. GetHarley operates both a patient-facing storefront and a practitioner platform used by clinicians to manage recommendations, orders, and client relationships. Backed by Index Ventures, the company addresses concerns such as acne, fine lines, pigmentation, and ageing. As of this profile, GetHarley does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or an MCP server; this record captures its identity, web properties, and probed domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Tooth Fairy
providers.description: Toothfairy is a UK dental telehealth platform billing itself as the world's first dentist on-demand, pairing registered dentists with a consumer mobile app to deliver teeth straightening with clear aligners, prescription teeth whitening, and same-day emergency video dental consultations 24/7, plus employer dental plans for businesses. The company is health-regulated in the UK, backed by Seedcamp, and ships its product as iOS and Android apps with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Gousto
providers.description: Gousto is a British meal-kit retailer founded in 2012 by Timo Boldt and James Carter and headquartered in Shepherd's Bush, London. It delivers recipe boxes with pre-portioned fresh ingredients and step-by-step recipes to homes across the UK, using proprietary data science, ERP, courier-integration and warehouse-automation systems to run its subscription operation. A SoftBank Vision Fund portfolio company, Gousto does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public digital surface (website, engineering blog, GitHub organization, and coordinated vulnerability-disclosure program) for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Acturis
providers.description: Acturis is a United Kingdom insurance software company founded in 2000 by David McDonald and Theo Duchen, operating the UK's leading multi-tenant SaaS platform for general insurance brokers, insurers and MGAs. The Acturis system covers commercial and personal lines broking, e-trade and digital distribution, policy administration, claims, document management, premium finance and accounting, and it builds and runs eight of the top ten UK insurer extranets. Acturis Group extends the platform into Germany, France and Canada (through the acquisitions of Power Broker and Brovada) and reports over 100,000 users across more than 40 countries. Its API posture is partner-gated and honestly not developer-facing: acturis.com markets an "API-enabled platform" and "API capabilities" but publishes no developer portal, no API reference, no OpenAPI or Swagger definition, and no self-serve onboarding. developer.acturis.com, developers.acturis.com, docs.acturis.com and api.acturis.com do not resolve, and /developers, /api, /developer and /integrations all return 404. Real integration happens through commercial agreements — insurer extranet and e-trade connections, the Polaris imarket digital-trading standards Acturis has traded on since 2005, and named bilateral work such as the Aviva claims Broker API launched in December 2024, which brokers enable through an Aviva Claims Service Manager or an Acturis Account Manager rather than through any public signup.

providers.name: Concirrus
providers.description: Concirrus Ltd is a London-headquartered insurtech founded in 2012 that builds AI-driven underwriting software for the specialty and commercial insurance market — marine (hull, cargo, P&I), aviation, construction, property, and political violence and terrorism. Its platform (Quest, Marine One, the Underwriting Workbench, Exposure Management, Loss Run Intelligence, and an "Enterprise Model" universal submission-ingestion layer) ingests broker submissions, structures the risk data, scores behavioural risk, and returns rating and exposure decisions to carriers, MGAs and brokers — much of it aimed at the Lloyd's and London subscription market. Concirrus is a vendor to insurers rather than an insurer itself, so it touches quote and rating rather than bind, issue or FNOL. Its API posture is partner-gated: marketing describes "a modular, API first platform" and "seamless integration with London Market platforms", but as of 2026-07-25 there is no public developer portal, no published API reference, no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger, no Postman collection, and no public GraphQL or webhook catalog. Every developer and docs hostname probed (developer./developers./docs./api. on both concirrus.com and concirrus.ai) does not resolve, and every on-site developer path returns 404. Integration is obtained through a commercial engagement or the partner ecosystem programme, not self-serve signup. No ACORD, AL3, NGDS or ACORD XML reference appears anywhere on the public site. Concirrus does publish a real compliance posture: in August 2025 it announced ISO/IEC 42001 (AI management), ISO/IEC 27001 (information security) and SOC 2 certification, claiming to be the first insurtech to hold all three — though no trust center or downloadable report accompanies the announcement.

providers.name: MyBuilder
providers.description: MyBuilder is a UK online marketplace that connects homeowners with local, reviewed tradespeople for home improvement, repair and maintenance work. Founded in 2004 by stonemason Ryan Notz and headquartered in London, the platform lets homeowners post a job for free, review interested tradespeople by their profiles, work history and customer feedback, and shortlist the ones they want to hire. Tradespeople browse leads for free and pay a fee only when a customer shortlists them. MyBuilder was acquired by IAC's HomeAdvisor in 2017 and now operates as part of the Instapro Group of European home-services marketplaces. MyBuilder is a consumer-facing web platform and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public identity, security and domain posture.

providers.name: DoorFeed
providers.description: DoorFeed is a technology-led residential real estate investment platform, founded in 2021 and headquartered in Paris, that helps institutional investors, funds, and family offices source and manage single-family rental portfolios at scale across the UK and France. The platform ingests roughly 150,000 new property listings and over 1,000,000 property images every day, structuring market data, comparable transactions, valuation signals, and energy-performance data into a single acquisition and asset-management workflow that takes investors from market screening to investment decision in minutes. DoorFeed is backed by HV Capital, Seedcamp, and Motive Partners. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead and enriched by the pipeline; DoorFeed publishes no public API or developer program at this time.

providers.name: Kestrl: Muslim Money App
providers.description: Kestrl is a UK-based, FCA-regulated ethical fintech offering a values-aligned money app for Muslim and ethically-minded consumers. In partnership with Maybank Islamic, it provides interest-free (Sharia-compliant) banking, a Mastercard debit card with values filtering, goal-based sub-accounts, interest purification and Zakat calculation, transaction monitoring that alerts users to payments toward ethically questionable companies, and security features such as card freezing and biometric authentication. Kestrl is a consumer mobile application on iOS and Android; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched from public web sources.

providers.name: Fuse
providers.description: Fuse Energy is a UK retail energy supplier providing gas and electricity to homes and businesses, alongside EV charging, solar and battery storage tracking with grid export, and smart home energy management. The company emphasises savings against the UK price cap, a fast (~3 minute) online sign-up, automated supplier switching, and 24/7 customer support including an AI assistant called "Plugs". Fuse was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and Speedinvest and added to the API Evangelist network. It operates a consumer/business energy web and mobile experience and does not publish a public developer API program at this time.

providers.name: Fuse Energy
providers.description: Fuse Energy (Fuse Energy Supply Limited) is a UK-based residential and business energy supplier providing gas and electricity on variable, fixed, and multi-rate tariffs, alongside EV charging, solar and battery export tracking, multi-property account management, and an in-app AI energy assistant called Plugs. The company positions itself around beating the UK energy price cap, sign-up in under three minutes, and 24-hour customer support. It operates a consumer- and business-facing web and mobile app experience and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: OakNorth
providers.description: OakNorth is a UK-based commercial bank and business-lending institution founded in 2015, providing debt financing to mid-market and lower-mid-market businesses in the UK and, through its New York team, the United States. Its products span business loans (from roughly GBP 1m to tens of millions), commercial real estate lending, commercial & industrial cash-flow financing, fund finance, and business and personal savings accounts. OakNorth is backed by the SoftBank Vision Fund. It publicly exposes no developer API, open-banking API, or developer portal; its public technical surface is limited to a HackerOne responsible-disclosure program and standard web/legal properties. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Electric Car Scheme
providers.description: The Electric Car Scheme is a UK B Corp providing electric vehicle salary sacrifice as an employee benefit. Employees lease any electric car of their choice with the monthly cost deducted from gross salary before Income Tax and National Insurance, saving 20-50% versus a personal lease, while employers save on Class 1A National Insurance. Packages are all-inclusive (lease, insurance, maintenance, servicing and breakdown) with Complete Protection covering employees who leave partway through a lease term. The company integrates with employer payroll systems via API or SFTP and offers Single Sign-On for employees, plus an included Charge Scheme for charging access.

providers.name: Bonnet
providers.description: Bonnet is a UK-based electric vehicle (EV) charging app that aggregates multiple charging networks into a single platform, letting drivers find, access, and pay for chargers across Europe through one membership. Headquartered in Bristol and acquired by OVO Energy, it gives consumers real-time charger status, route planning, membership plans with per-charge savings, and weekly charging-credit rewards, while offering charge point operator (CPO) and fleet solutions with white-label integration for businesses. Surfaced as a portfolio company of gv and lightspeed-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Bonnet publishes a consumer mobile app but no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: IHG Hotels & Resorts
providers.description: InterContinental Hotels Group PLC (trading as IHG Hotels & Resorts) is a British asset-light hotel group headquartered at Windsor Dials, 1 Arthur Road, Windsor, Berkshire SL4 1RS, United Kingdom, with an Americas office at 3 Ravinia Drive, Atlanta, Georgia. Its own corporate site states 7,014 hotels and 1,035,589 rooms across more than 100 countries, around 400,000 colleagues, 20 brands and the IHG One Rewards loyalty programme (figures read from ihgplc.com on 2026-07-28). The brand portfolio spans Six Senses, Regent, InterContinental, Vignette Collection, Kimpton, Hotel Indigo, voco, HUALUXE, Crowne Plaza, EVEN Hotels, Holiday Inn, Holiday Inn Express, Holiday Inn Resorts, Holiday Inn Club Vacations, Garner, avid, Atwell Suites, Staybridge Suites, Candlewood Suites, IHG Army Hotels and Iberostar Beachfront Resorts. In the distribution chain IHG sits on the supply side as a franchisor and manager rather than an owner: it aggregates independently owned and operated properties into a single central reservation system and pushes that inventory out through its own ihg.com and app direct channels, through the three GDSs and their agency terminals, through OTAs and wholesalers, and through corporate and group channels. Critically, IHG does not run its own reservation platform any more. It announced a partnership with Amadeus in 2015 to build a cloud Guest Reservation System to replace HOLIDEX, its proprietary system in service since 1965, and migrated onto it across 2018 and early 2019 — so the hotel group most likely to be a lock-in vendor is itself a customer of a GDS company's platform, and group bookings land in Amadeus Delphi and Meeting Broker. Its API posture, stated honestly, is gated and undocumented. There is no live developer portal. The one that existed — PartnerConnect RoomService at pcroomservice.ihg.com, a TIBCO Mashery portal publishing five rate, availability and hotel-content APIs — is decommissioned: the hostname is NXDOMAIN on Google, Cloudflare and Quad9 resolvers as of 2026-07-28 and the Internet Archive holds no page capture after 2019. What remains live is partnerconnect.ihg.com (HTTP 200), an affiliate marketing programme whose signup routes to Commission Junction and which still advertises "access to real-time hotel rates, availability and hotel content API's" without linking to any technical resource. Real API hostnames exist — api.ihg.com CNAMEs to ihg.api.mashery.com with an sb-ihg.mashery.com sandbox, and apis.ihg.com, b2b.ihg.com, mcp.ihg.com, booking.ihg.com and concerto.ihg.com all sit behind Akamai — but every one returns 403 Access Denied or 401 on every path probed, including /openapi.json, /swagger.json, /api-docs and /.well-known/. No OpenAPI, Swagger, AsyncAPI, GraphQL SDL, WSDL, XSD, OpenTravel/OTA or HTNG reference is published anywhere by IHG. apis[] is deliberately empty: listing an Akamai-gated hostname or a decommissioned 2017 portal as a live API would be fabrication. The value of this record is the switchingCost block in review.yml, which captures what published IHG documents actually say about what it costs to leave — including the archived RoomService Terms of Use classing "API parameters" as Confidential Information and binding partners to the Master PartnerConnect Terms and Conditions plus the Six Continents Hotels E-commerce Master Service Agreement, and the current IHG One Rewards member terms stating that members whose accounts are cancelled "by IHG or by the Member, will forfeit all Points, Point vouchers, Reward Nights, and any other benefits associated with the account".

providers.name: Tuli
providers.description: Tuli Health operates a UK-wide network of over 300 high-street pharmacies as local diagnostic hubs, making clinical services - primarily blood testing and phlebotomy - accessible in every neighbourhood so people can get care close to home. It offers healthcare providers three models - One Network (white-label phlebotomy), One Solution (end-to-end test kits, draws and lab analysis), and an Enterprise tier with custom integration. Tuli exposes an API and web portal for booking and managing tests, though public developer documentation is not yet published.

providers.name: On the Beach
providers.description: On the Beach Group plc (LSE: OTB) is a Manchester-headquartered online travel agent and the United Kingdom's largest online short-haul beach package holiday specialist, founded in 2004 by Simon Cooper and registered at Aeroworks, 5 Adair Street, Manchester M1 2NQ. It sits on the demand side of the travel distribution chain: an asset-light dynamic packager that buys real-time seats from 42 airlines and hotel inventory from bedbanks and direct hotel contracts, combines them into ATOL-protected packages, and sells them direct to UK and Republic of Ireland consumers through onthebeach.co.uk, sunshine.co.uk and its mobile app. FY25 total transaction value was GBP 1.25bn across 1.7 million customers. It is a consumer of other operators' distribution APIs rather than a publisher of its own - it was the first UK OTA to take a direct NDC connection to Emirates' Online B2B API in 2019 and signed a direct Ryanair "Approved OTA" partnership in 2024 - and it explicitly bypasses the GDS layer entirely. Its API posture as a producer is almost non-existent. The FY25 results describe an "API-first microservices architecture" and a proprietary Hotel Discovery Cache managing more than 5 billion hotel prices, but none of that surface is published: there is no developer portal, no API documentation, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, no partner or trade API, and no self-serve access of any kind. Its only remaining B2B channel, Classic Collection, was put into orderly wind-down on 23 September 2025. The single exception, and the first externally addressable machine surface the company has ever shipped, is a ChatGPT App launched on 1 April 2026 - claimed as the first by a UK OTA - which serves live, bookable package combinations to ChatGPT users over MCP. That surface is distribution-gated rather than developer-facing: no endpoint, tool list, schema, auth flow or terms are documented, and a deliberate mcp.onthebeach.co.uk host exists but is Cloudflare WAF-blocked to every probe.

providers.name: Carmoola
providers.description: Carmoola is a UK-based, mobile-first car finance platform that lets consumers get a pre-approved budget in minutes through its app, then pay dealers or private sellers directly with a virtual card. It offers Hire Purchase (HP) and Personal Contract Purchase (PCP) financing, soft credit checks that do not affect the applicant's score, flexible repayment terms, and the ability to refinance an existing car loan. Carmoola is authorised and regulated by the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) and is backed by investors including QED Investors. This profile was surfaced as a QED Investors portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Carmoola operates a consumer app rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: flatfair
providers.description: flatfair is a UK-based tenancy deposit platform for letting agents, landlords, and Build-to-Rent operators, offering deposit alternatives and deposit administration products. Its products include No Deposit (tenants pay 28% of one month's rent plus VAT instead of a five-week cash deposit), Deposits, Unlock Deposits, Deposit Boost, tenant Referencing, and Tenant Guarantor. flatfair is used by more than 850 agents and Build-to-Rent operators to reduce move-in friction and cut deposit administration time by around 60 minutes per tenancy. The company operates a web application for agents and tenants but does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: INBOTIQA
providers.description: INBOTIQA is a UK-based fintech whose flagship product, YUDOmail, is an Intelligent Business Email and shared-mailbox management platform for high-volume group inboxes at banks, BPOs and financial-services operations teams. YUDOmail layers over Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace to turn incoming emails into assigned, trackable tasks with ownership, due dates, SLA tracking, machine-learning triage and sentiment analysis, audit trails and analytics, without replacing the underlying email platform. It deploys in the cloud or on-premises, integrates with Symphony chat and Microsoft Teams, and is used across KYC, FX, collateral, settlements and trade-support functions. INBOTIQA was a 2019 Barclays Accelerator (powered by Techstars) company.

providers.name: Josh Wood Colour
providers.description: Josh Wood Colour is a UK-based at-home hair colour brand founded by celebrity colourist Josh Wood, selling permanent and semi-permanent hair dye, root touch-up, gloss, toners, blonde and grey-blending products, and haircare direct to consumers through a Shopify-powered online store at joshwoodcolour.com. The brand pairs its retail catalogue with a free personalised colour-matching consultation service and editorial hair-care advice. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Index Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As a consumer retail e-commerce brand it exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface; this profile captures its web identity, security posture, and customer-facing properties.

providers.name: London House Exchange (Property Partner)
providers.description: London House Exchange, formerly Property Partner, is an FCA-regulated online platform that operates the world's only regulated exchange for individual residential, student and commercial properties. Founded in 2014 and now owned by US digital homeownership company Better, the platform lets retail investors buy fractional shares in professionally managed UK properties, earn monthly dividends from rental income, and trade those shares with other investors on a secondary market. It also offers property-backed mortgage bonds, an ISA, and bridging finance, with over £100m of fractionalised property assets under management and thousands of investors across more than 80 countries. It was surfaced as a Seedcamp portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Sidekick
providers.description: Sidekick is a UK-based online wealth management and investing platform that offers expert-led investments and savings products once reserved for the ultra-wealthy, delivered through a mobile app and web platform. Its product range spans managed investment portfolios, savings accounts, private equity access, and cryptocurrency exposure. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Seedcamp, Sidekick is a consumer (B2C) fintech and publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation as of this enrichment pass.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Vodafone
providers.description: Vodafone Group plc is a UK-headquartered (Newbury, England) multinational telecommunications company and one of the world's largest mobile and fixed network operators, with operations in 15 country markets and partner-market agreements covering 40+ additional countries across Europe and Africa. The group serves 279 million mobile customers, 5 million business customers, and manages 215+ million IoT connections through its Vodafone IoT platform. Beyond mobile and broadband connectivity, Vodafone operates one of the largest IoT/M2M businesses in the industry, invests in 70+ subsea cables, and runs financial services like M-PESA (Africa) and Vodapay. Through Vodafone Business it sells connectivity, cloud, security, and managed-mobility services to enterprises, and through the GSMA Open Gateway and CAMARA initiative it exposes a growing portfolio of standardised network APIs (Number Verify, SIM Swap, Quality on Demand, Device Location, Match, MVNO Discovery, and more) via the Vodafone Developer Marketplace (developer.vodafone.com), which publishes 27+ commercial and CAMARA APIs across Identity, Mobile, Analytics, Boost/QoS, and Partner categories. The Marketplace exposes sandbox and live endpoints under api-sandbox.vf-dmp.engineering.vodafone.com and api.vf-dmp.engineering.vodafone.com, with OAuth2 (Consumer Key / Consumer Secret) authentication and Postman collections for every product. Vodafone is a premier member of the CAMARA alliance hosted at the Linux Foundation, a founding participant in the GSMA Open Gateway, and one of the principal telco operators driving network-as-an-API adoption globally.

providers.name: Healthera
providers.description: Healthera is a United Kingdom digital-health and patient-engagement company, founded in 2015 by Cambridge University students and headquartered in Cambridge, England. It runs a patient-facing pharmacy app and website for ordering NHS prescriptions and medicines online and booking pharmacy services (Pharmacy First, treatments, vaccinations), alongside a pharmacy-facing SaaS "Patient Experience Platform" used by 1,700+ community pharmacies to manage repeat prescriptions, bookings, marketing, and delivery. In November 2022 Healthera became the first pharmacy app to integrate with the NHS Electronic Prescription Service (EPS), and it connects to NHS Digital / NHS England systems plus third-party platforms such as myGP, eConsult, Cegedim Rx Pharmacy Manager, Medpoint, Royal Mail, and Uber for same-hour delivery. Healthera markets custom integration APIs to pharmacy and brand partners, but as of this review it publishes no public developer portal, no self-serve API documentation, and no machine-readable contract; its api.healthera.co.uk "Healthera Core" host is a private backend and exposes no FHIR CapabilityStatement. Integration is partner-gated rather than self-serve.

providers.name: Tripledot
providers.description: Tripledot Studios (Tripledot Group) is a London-headquartered mobile games developer and publisher focused on data-driven casual games, with chart-topping titles including Woodoku, Solitaire, Duplica, Wordhop, Solitaire Scapes, Sudoku, Spider Solitaire and Blackjack played by more than 25 million daily active users. Founded as an independent studio and named Best Developer at the Pocket Gamer Mobile Games Awards 2023, Tripledot closed an $800 million acquisition of AppLovin's mobile games studio portfolio (ten studios) on July 1, 2025, and is backed by investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners. Tripledot publishes no first-party developer API, portal or SDKs, but its website ships a real llms.txt and a live, publicly connectable MCP endpoint (the Wix Site Visitor Assistant) for agentic access to site content.

providers.name: 01health
providers.description: 01Health is a UK-based health technology company building clinical infrastructure that lets specialist healthcare be delivered safely inside community and dental clinics rather than only in hospitals. Founded in 2022 by Dr Sonia Szamocki, its platform centralizes patient acquisition, clinical protocols, remote specialist oversight, treatment workflows, procurement, and financial management into a single system, currently spanning orthodontics (32Co) and sleep medicine (Aerox). 01Health is backed by Balderton Capital, Gresham House Ventures, Eka Ventures, and Wavemaker360. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal has been published to date; this profile captures the company identity and the security posture of its public web surface.

providers.name: Smol
providers.description: Smol is a UK-based direct-to-consumer home-care brand founded in 2018 by Paula Quazi and Nick Green, delivering concentrated, plant-based, cruelty-free cleaning products — laundry capsules, dishwasher tablets, fabric conditioner, surface sprays and personal-care bars — on a flexible subscription that ships refills through the letterbox. The company positions itself as a sustainability challenger to legacy home-care brands, emphasizing reduced plastic, carbon and chemical load, and became a certified B Corporation in July 2022. Backed by Balderton Capital and GV, Smol operates a consumer e-commerce and subscription business; it publishes no public developer API, SDKs or developer program.

providers.name: Nutmeg (J.P. Morgan Personal Investing)
providers.description: Nutmeg is a UK digital wealth manager and robo-advisor founded in 2011 and acquired by JPMorgan Chase in 2021, now operating as J.P. Morgan Personal Investing. It offers consumer investment accounts including Stocks and Shares ISAs, Lifetime ISAs, Junior ISAs, personal pensions, and general investment accounts, with fully managed, Smart Alpha, socially responsible, thematic, fixed allocation, and income portfolio strategies plus free financial guidance and paid advice. Nutmeg is authorised and regulated by the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA register #552016). It is a consumer-facing wealth platform and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Plum
providers.description: Plum is a UK-based personal finance "money app" that helps consumers save and invest automatically. Its mobile app pairs automated savings algorithms (eight saving automations) with a range of regulated products including Easy Access Savings, a Cash ISA, a 95-day Notice Account, a money-market Interest pocket, a Stocks & Shares ISA, a Self-Invested Personal Pension (SIPP), and access to thousands of stocks and funds. Plum operates under FCA oversight through multiple entities covering payment services, e-money, investment broking, and account information services, and monetizes via subscription tiers (Basic, Plus, Boost, Max). It is a consumer-facing product with no public developer API; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Partech and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Popsa
providers.description: Popsa is a UK-based, mobile-first photo printing company that uses AI to help customers create photo books, calendars, prints, tiles, boxes and ornaments in minutes. Founded in the UK and a certified B Corporation that offsets 100% of production and shipping carbon emissions, Popsa serves over 10 million customers and ships to more than 50 countries with localised storefronts across Europe, North America and Australia. Its differentiators are AI-powered automatic layouts, generative captions, facial recognition, print-quality scoring and dynamic colour themes, delivering an average five-minute creation time. Popsa was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes no public developer API, SDK or developer portal; this profile captures its public discovery surface (llms.txt, security.txt) and domain security posture instead.

providers.name: Numan
providers.description: Numan (trading as Vir Health Limited) is a UK-based digital healthcare and telemedicine company offering convenient, clinician-led care direct to consumers. Its services span weight-loss programmes (including GLP-1 medications such as Mounjaro and Wegovy), men's health (erectile dysfunction, hair loss, testosterone), women's health (menopause support), at-home blood tests and diagnostics, supplements, and one-off doctor consultations, delivered through its website and iOS/Android app. Numan is regulated by the Care Quality Commission and operates a GPhC-licensed pharmacy. It is a portfolio company of Anthemis. As of this enrichment pass Numan publishes no public developer API, SDKs, MCP server, or partner integration surface.

providers.name: Savills
providers.description: Savills plc is a London-headquartered global real estate advisor, established in 1855, listed on the London Stock Exchange, with more than 42,000 people in over 70 countries. It sits on the advisory side of the property value chain rather than the data-platform side: commercial and prime residential agency, transaction advisory and capital markets, valuation and professional services, building and project consultancy, property and facilities management, rural and agricultural advisory, occupier services, the Savills Research publication programme, and a separate fund manager in Savills Investment Management. Its home market is the United Kingdom, where there is no MLS and no cooperative listing standard — residential stock reaches consumers through the Rightmove and Zoopla duopoly by way of agency CRM software (Reapit, Alto, Street, Apex27) rather than a shared cooperative pool. Savills is a supplier into that pipe, not an operator of it. Its API posture is the honest null case for this sector. Savills publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDK, no Postman collection and no machine-readable contract of any kind: developer., developers., docs. and apis.savills.com do not resolve, /developers, /api, /docs, /openapi.json, /swagger.json and /api-docs on savills.com, savills.co.uk and savills.us all return 404, and no OpenID Connect discovery document is served. Undocumented internal service hosts do exist behind the consumer property search — livev6-searchapi, livev6-authentication and livev6-profile.savills.com, named in the search application's own endpoints.js — but every one of them returns 404 to an anonymous client and none is described anywhere public. There is no RESO Web API or Data Dictionary certification, no OData $metadata document and no Universal Property Identifier anywhere in the Savills estate; RESO is a North American NAR/MLS construct and the UK has nothing to certify against. Savills publishes no open data either — its research output is PDF and web narrative, and the genuinely open UK property layer belongs to the public sector (HM Land Registry Price Paid Data and Ordnance Survey), not to the brokerage. For a developer there is no gate to pass, because there is no door: the only published route is the corporate contact form.

providers.name: Atom Bank
providers.description: Atom Bank plc is a UK app-only digital bank headquartered in Newcastle upon Tyne, and the first mobile-only bank in the United Kingdom (no branches, no web banking). Authorised by the Prudential Regulation Authority and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FS Register 661960), Atom offers fixed savings accounts, residential and commercial mortgages, and secured business lending, all delivered through its iOS and Android apps. Atom does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; it is a consumer of UK Open Banking, letting customers share a one-off snapshot of their bank data (via aggregators such as Plaid, Tink and TrueLayer) to speed lending decisions. Backed by Anthemis and others, Atom runs a Go/Python/Java/Kafka technology stack and operates a four-day working week.

providers.name: Second Nature
providers.description: Second Nature is a UK-based digital weight-loss programme that combines NHS-trusted, CQC-regulated clinical care with dietitian-led coaching and behaviour-change support. The service pairs weight-loss medication (including Wegovy, Mounjaro, oral semaglutide and Orlistat programmes) with personalised medication reviews, a mobile app for tracking, and a science-based content library of guides and member stories. It operates as a registered pharmacy, supports NHS referrals and partnerships, and was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Speedinvest. As of this enrichment pass Second Nature publishes a consumer marketing site and an llms.txt discovery file but exposes no public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Yonder
providers.description: Yonder is a UK-based financial technology company offering rewards credit and debit cards — a "financial membership" that earns points on everyday spending, redeemable across 300+ dining, travel, shopping, entertainment and wellness partners. Cards run on the Mastercard network with no foreign-exchange fees, and Yonder is authorised and regulated by the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) with FSCS-protected accounts held via partner banks. Yonder ships a consumer mobile app and a help centre but does not expose a public developer API or portal. Added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead (backers include Northzone, Seedcamp and Techstars).

providers.name: Reposit
providers.description: Reposit is a UK-based PropTech and fintech company offering a deposit alternative for the residential rental market. Instead of paying a traditional cash deposit, tenants pay a one-time, non-refundable fee (typically one week's rent) for insurance-backed cover, while landlords and letting agents receive protection worth up to eight weeks' rent. The FCA-authorised product is underwritten by a leading insurer and serves letting agents, build-to-rent (BTR) operators, landlords and tenants, with integrations into common property management tools. This profile was surfaced as a Seedcamp portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Reposit publishes no public developer API surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Superscript
providers.description: Superscript is a UK- and Netherlands-based business insurance provider offering flexible, subscription-based cover for small and growing businesses, sole traders, landlords, and larger enterprises. Its product range spans public and employers' liability, professional indemnity, cyber insurance, landlord insurance, and industry-specific policies, sold direct and through a broker channel. Superscript was surfaced as a portfolio company of Seedcamp and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, or programmatic integration surface; this profile captures its public web identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: So Sure
providers.description: So Sure (wearesosure.com), operated by Open Insurance Services UK Limited, was a UK app-based social insurance provider offering mobile phone and home contents insurance, known for a social/peer insurance model that rewarded claim-free groups. It was an early portfolio company of 500 Global. The company has stopped selling new policies and has transitioned its mobile phone cover to the Huddle Insurance brand while continuing to service existing customers. So Sure publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, or technical documentation surface.

providers.name: Medefer
providers.description: Medefer is a UK digital-first managed clinical services company that connects patients directly with consultant specialists remotely and safely, working in partnership with the NHS. Its virtual, consultant-led model triages and manages patient referrals through remote review, coordinating in-person tests and treatment through a trusted local and national partner network only when they are needed. Backed by Seedcamp, Medefer brings hospital-level specialist expertise into patients' homes and communities, reducing waiting times for NHS and self-pay patients across a range of specialties. Medefer operates a patient/clinician application and a private internal application backend (api.medefer.com) rather than a public developer API program.

providers.name: Sano
providers.description: Sano Genetics is a UK-based precision-medicine company operating a 360-degree platform that connects the workflows behind decentralized clinical trials and research studies. Its services span patient recruitment and outreach, protocol and study design, digital prescreening and consent, electronic medical record retrieval, at-home DNA testing with genetic counseling, participant engagement portals, and biomarker testing programs.
