The platform helps pharmaceutical sponsors and research teams find, engage, and retain the right participants for genetically-informed studies. Surfaced as a Seedcamp portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API is published at this time.

providers.name: IMP Software
providers.description: IMP Software builds MAT-first financial management software for the UK education sector. Its flagship product, IMP Planner, is a single-database, trust-wide platform for budgeting, forecasting, reporting, Integrated Curriculum Financial Planning (ICFP) and purchasing, used by Multi-Academy Trusts (MATs) and their schools. Based in Exeter, UK, the company is trusted by more than 550 trusts across roughly 6,000 schools and secured a growth investment from Partech in September 2025. IMP Planner is a closed SaaS application for trust finance teams; IMP Software does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: The Modern Milkman
providers.description: The Modern Milkman is a UK doorstep delivery service that brings farm-fresh milk, groceries and household essentials to customers in returnable and reusable glass bottles or recyclable packaging, with flexible ordering and early-morning delivery. Founded to modernise the traditional milkround, the company focuses on reducing food waste and single-use plastic through a return-and-reuse model, local sourcing, and a subscription-style ordering experience delivered through its website and mobile apps. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The company publishes no public developer API, but does maintain an llms.txt for AI agents, a customer help centre, and a blog. Sector: consumer / direct-to-consumer grocery delivery.

providers.name: Carwow
providers.description: Carwow is a UK-based online automotive marketplace that helps consumers buy, sell, lease, and finance cars without haggling or hidden fees. Buyers browse new and used car deals, compare dealer quotes, arrange leasing (including salary sacrifice and fleet through Carwow Leasey), find electric-vehicle deals, and access vehicle financing and credit brokering. Sellers get free car valuations, part-exchange, and van sales. Carwow also publishes professional car reviews and ratings, runs a large YouTube channel, and offers comparison tools, EV charging maps, a car history checker, and insurance services. Founded in London and backed by Accel, Balderton Capital, and Bessemer Venture Partners, Carwow operates across the UK and Europe. It maintains a public GitHub organization of open-source engineering tooling but does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Close Brothers
providers.description: Close Brothers Group plc (LSE: CBG) is a UK merchant banking group founded in 1878 and a constituent of the FTSE 250 Index, headquartered at 10 Crown Place, London EC2A 4FT. The group provides specialist lending across motor, premium, asset, invoice, and property finance; takes personal and business deposits through Close Brothers Savings; manages wealth through Close Brothers Asset Management; and trades securities through Winterflood. Its banking entity, Close Brothers Limited, is authorised by the Prudential Regulation Authority and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority and the PRA. Close Brothers is not one of the CMA9 mandated banks; it offers savings and deposit products rather than online payment (current) accounts, and therefore carries no UK Open Banking (OBIE / PSD2) Read/Write or Open Data publishing obligation. As of this profile no public developer portal, Open Banking Open Data endpoint, or documented API surface could be confirmed for the group.

providers.name: Open Bionics
providers.description: Open Bionics is a Bristol, UK-based medical technology company that designs and manufactures advanced multi-grip bionic arms for children and adults with upper-limb differences. Its Hero product family (Hero ARM, Hero PRO, Hero RGD, Hero FLEX and Hero GAUNTLET) pairs 3D-printed, lightweight myoelectric prosthetic hands with an ecosystem of MyoPods wireless electrodes and the Sidekick companion app, delivered through a network of specialist prosthetists and clinics in the US and UK. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company; enrichment probing found no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or event surface.

providers.name: Push Doctor
providers.description: Push Doctor is a UK telehealth company offering video consultations with licensed UK GPs via smartphone, describing itself as the UK's first platform to provide video doctor consultations on mobile. It serves both NHS patients and private paying customers, covering online GP appointments, digital prescriptions, referrals and follow-up care. Headquartered in Manchester and backed by Partech, Push Doctor operates as a consumer-facing telemedicine service; no public developer API, developer portal, or SDK surface was found during enrichment probes.

providers.name: Cera
providers.description: Cera is a United Kingdom-based digital-first home healthcare company, founded in 2016 and headquartered in London, that describes itself as Europe's largest provider of in-home care. Cera delivers home care, live-in care, nurse-led and complex care, extra-care housing, supported living, and specialist learning-disability and autism support, all wrapped around a proprietary digital platform that uses data analytics and machine learning so its network of carers can collect, monitor, and react to vital-sign and health-condition changes in real time. Cera positions this technology as a remote-monitoring and predictive layer that surfaces deterioration in health earlier and reduces hospitalisations across its United Kingdom home-care operations. As of this review Cera exposes no public developer portal, no self-serve REST API, and no HL7 FHIR endpoint or CapabilityStatement; its platform is an internal, operator-facing product delivered through consumer and carer mobile apps rather than a documented partner API. This profile is an honest identity-only stub recording the absence of a public API surface for a United Kingdom telehealth-adjacent home-care provider.

providers.name: Lottie
providers.description: Lottie is a UK-based later-life care marketplace that helps families and retirees find and fund the country's best care homes, home care providers, and retirement living communities. The free consumer service matches people with regulated care providers, publishes availability and pricing, and offers guidance from care experts alongside a large library of funding and care guides. Backed by Accel and General Catalyst, Lottie serves tens of thousands of families monthly across England, Scotland, and Wales. As of this enrichment pass the company operates a consumer-facing web platform only and publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal.

providers.name: Dwelly
providers.description: Dwelly (legal entity PROSPIRE TECHNOLOGIES LTD, also trading as Dwelly Group) is a UK-based, AI-first lettings and property-management company founded in 2023 by Ilya Drozdov (CEO), Dan Lifshits (CPO) and Dmitry Khanukov (CTO). Rather than selling software, Dwelly grows by acquiring independent UK lettings agencies and succession-planning their owners out, then running the acquired books on its own AI-powered operating platform. That platform automates tenant find (self-service enquiry chat, virtual viewings, verified offers), banking-grade tenant screening (KYC, Right to Rent, referencing), Direct Debit rent collection with automatic reconciliation and arrears handling, maintenance and property management workflows with centralised communications, and continuous lettings compliance. Dwelly is backed by General Catalyst, Begin Capital and S16VC. As of this profile Dwelly publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs or technical documentation — the platform is operated internally for its own and its acquired agencies' portfolios.

providers.name: Laelaps AI
providers.description: Laelaps AI is a Zurich- and UK-based autonomous security company building what it calls "the brain behind security" — a hardware-agnostic, fail-safe autonomy layer that unifies aerial, ground, and stationary robots together with a site's existing fixed cameras into a single coordinated monitoring force. The platform pairs field foundational models and visual intelligence with multi-agent coordination so that critical infrastructure and commercial and defense sites can be watched continuously, incidents detected and triaged automatically, and robots dispatched to observe and deter without a human operator watching every screen. Founded by Dr. Sophia Belser (CEO), Dr. Maria "Mania" Stamatopoulou (CRO), and Rokas Bendikas (CTO), the company is backed by Speedinvest, Expeditions Fund, Florent Venture Partners, Fund F, ESA BIC Switzerland, and NVIDIA Inception. As of this profile Laelaps AI publishes a three-page corporate website and no public developer surface — no documentation, API reference, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts were found.

providers.name: Tiney
providers.description: Tiney is the UK's fastest-growing Ofsted-approved childminder agency, connecting parents with quality-assured home childminders and supporting educators through training, registration, and ongoing quality assurance. Operating as a government-regulated Childminder Agency (CMA), tiney runs a consumer marketplace plus a mobile app for finding local childcare and managing payments, communication, and children's learning updates. Tiney publishes no public developer API; its backend at api.tiney.co powers the parent and childminder apps and is access-restricted (HTTP 403) and undocumented.

providers.name: Chipper Cash
providers.description: Chipper Cash is a pan-African fintech (legal entities Critical Ideas, Inc. and Voyse Technologies US, Inc.) operating a mobile-first cross-border money transfer, digital payments, crypto, and investing platform across Africa and the diaspora. Founded in 2018 by Ham Serunjogi (Uganda) and Maijid Moujaled (Ghana) after they met at Grinnell College in Iowa, Chipper became one of Africa's fintech unicorns in 2021 and has raised over $340M to date. The consumer app — available on iOS, Android, and web — supports peer-to-peer and cross-border transfers across 21+ African countries, virtual Visa cards (Chipper Card), bill pay and airtime top-ups, fractional US-stock investing (Chipper Stocks, 6,000+ public companies, from $1), and historically crypto trading (BTC/ETH). Reported scale includes 5M+ registered users, 1M+ Visa cards issued, and 250,000+ daily transactions. Direct consumer markets include Nigeria, Ghana, Uganda, Tanzania, South Africa, Rwanda, the UK, and the US. On the developer side, Chipper exposes the Chipper Network API ("Pay With Chipper") — a merchant-facing API that lets authorized businesses accept cross-border payments across 9 currencies, initiate payouts, issue refunds, and look up Chipper user accounts, authenticated with a Chipper User ID + Network API Key. Documentation is published as a Postman collection and access is gated by merchant onboarding; no public OpenAPI or open-source SDK is currently published. Adjacent products include Chipper ID (AI-led identity verification), Chipper Enterprise (bulk payments and collections), Business Accounts, and Zoona (agent-network remittances), plus an integration with TBD's tbDEX protocol for decentralized cross-border payments.

providers.name: Fractile
providers.description: Fractile is a UK-based semiconductor startup, founded in 2022 and headquartered in London with an engineering base in Bristol, designing a new class of AI inference processors. Its architecture physically interleaves memory and compute to overcome the memory-bandwidth bottleneck that limits large language model inference, targeting frontier model serving up to 25x faster and at roughly 1/10th the cost of existing hardware. The company takes a full-stack approach spanning transistor-level circuit design through cloud inference server logic, and in May 2026 raised $220M to build the next generation of inference hardware. Backers include Accel and Felicis. Led by founder and CEO Walter Goodwin, Fractile is a hardware/compute company and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Jade Autism
providers.description: Jade (Jade ND) is a Brazil-, UAE-, and UK-based education technology company building inclusive digital solutions for neurodivergent children, including those on the autism spectrum (ASD). Its product family includes Jade Edu (personalized-learning software for schools and educators), the Jade App (cognitive-development games for children, with 185,000+ downloads across 179 countries), Jade Astea (eye-tracking technology that assists professionals in evaluating autism-spectrum diagnosis), and Jade Academy (professional-development courses on inclusive and diverse education). Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Little Freddie
providers.description: Little Freddie (Sunny Fields Enterprise Ltd) is a UK-based organic baby and toddler food brand producing nutritious weaning products for infants from six months, developed with a paediatric dietitian to meet UK and EU baby-food guidelines. Its ranges include Greek-style yoghurts, Simply Fruit purees, Full of Veg meals, dairy-free alternatives, home-style meals and omega-3 "Good for Brains" options, sold through major UK retailers including Tesco, Sainsbury's, Asda, Morrisons, Co-op, Ocado, Booths and Spar. The company also runs a Parenting Hub with weaning, nutrition and parenting content. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Hillhouse; this profile currently exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: ProGrad
providers.description: ProGrad (prograd.uk) is a UK-based consumer mobile app that lets users earn money by playing games and completing online tasks such as surveys and offers, positioning itself as a leading "make money" app in the United Kingdom. Users choose from a large catalogue of games and micro-tasks, accumulate rewards, and withdraw earnings to PayPal or Visa once they pass a minimum threshold. The company also publishes Gen Z insights and research alongside a consumer blog. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network, ProGrad is a consumer-facing product with no public developer program, API portal, or programmatic surface at this time.

providers.name: Proportunity
providers.description: Proportunity is a London-based proptech/fintech mortgage lender, founded in 2016 by Vadim Toader and Stefan Boronea, that helps first-time buyers get onto the property ladder with a shared-equity loan. The Proportunity Loan supplements a buyer's deposit and can boost purchasing power by up to GBP 150,000, letting buyers secure a home with as little as a 5% deposit on any property on the market (not just new-builds). The company uses machine-learning models to forecast house prices and identify fair-valued homes in high-growth areas to reduce financing risk. Proportunity is authorised and regulated by the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FRN 716565). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Anthemis and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment found no public developer/API surface (consumer-facing product only).

providers.name: Truly Experiences
providers.description: Truly Experiences is a UK-based experiential gifting company that curates and sells memorable experiences as gifts rather than physical products. Its catalog spans dining, spa treatments, drinks tastings, activities, masterclasses, travel getaways, and premium "dreams come true" experiences, organized by recipient, occasion, price point, and UK location (London, Edinburgh, Birmingham, Manchester and beyond). After checkout customers receive an e-certificate with a unique code, and a concierge team arranges the booking date and time. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass it operates a consumer e-commerce storefront with no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Oxa
providers.description: Oxa (formerly Oxbotica, rebranded in 2023) is a British autonomous vehicle software company founded in 2014 in Oxford, England by Paul Newman and Ingmar Posner. Oxa builds what it calls Universal Autonomy — self-driving software configurable for almost any vehicle in almost any environment — and sells it as Industrial Mobility Automation for ports, airports, manufacturing yards, solar farms and shuttle networks. Its product line is Oxa Driver (the autonomy stack), Oxa Foundry (a generative-AI training and assurance toolchain, previously marketed as Oxa MetaDriver), Reference Autonomy Designs (modular hardware integration blueprints), and Oxa Hub (a cloud fleet-management suite covering remote assist, task design, workspace mapping, digital twins and in-use monitoring). Oxa Hub is described on the marketing site as offering "an API for optional integration with existing logistics systems", but Oxa publishes no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable specification on any public host. The company raised a $115M Series C in 2023 with participation from Google, and works with Ocado Group, ZF and bp.

providers.name: Evri
providers.description: Evri is the United Kingdom's largest dedicated parcel delivery company, formerly Hermes UK, headquartered in Leeds and majority owned by Apollo-managed funds. Following the CMA-cleared 2025 merger with DHL eCommerce UK, the combined group delivers more than a billion parcels a year across a courier network of 30,000+ couriers and van drivers, thousands of ParcelShops and lockers, and domestic, returns and international services for retailers and marketplace sellers. Evri sits at the last-mile end of the supply chain — the carrier a shipper, retailer or e-commerce platform hands a parcel to for final delivery in the UK. Its API posture is customer-contract portal only: Evri publishes no developer portal, no public API reference and no machine-readable specification. The host api.evri.com resolves to a live Tyk API Gateway (5.13.0) whose only publicly reachable path is an unauthenticated health check; every other probed path returns 404 and no listen path is discoverable without credentials. Shipment, label, ParcelShop, Print in Store and tracking credentials are issued by an Evri account manager or sales representative to contracted Corporate or Business accounts, with sandbox and production credentials handed over by email. In practice most integrators reach Evri indirectly through shipping-API aggregators such as EasyPost, ShipEngine / ShipStation, Sendcloud, AfterShip and Intersoft Sapient rather than directly.

providers.name: Fuse Energy
providers.description: Fuse Energy (originally launched as Tesseract) is a UK-based, vertically integrated energy supplier founded by former Revolut executives Alan Chang and Charles Orr. It buys power from generators and supplies gas and electricity directly to residential and business customers, positioning itself to beat the UK price cap with variable, fixed and multi-rate tariffs, 30-minute billing updates, EV charging, solar/battery export tracking and an in-app AI assistant called "Plugs." The company raised $78M led by Balderton Capital and Lakestar. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; as of this enrichment pass Fuse Energy publishes only a consumer-facing web and mobile app and no public developer API, SDK, or documentation.

providers.name: Sixfold
providers.description: Sixfold is a New York City-headquartered AI company building purpose-built artificial intelligence for insurance underwriting across Property & Casualty and Life & Health lines. Founded by Alex Schmelkin (CEO, previously co-founder of Unqork), Jane Tran (COO), and Brian Moseley (CTO, previously Head of Developer Experience at American Express), Sixfold processes unstructured submissions, automates risk research, produces appetite fit scores, generates cited case narratives, and applies underwriting guidelines consistently across submissions. The platform classifies risk using industry standards (SIC, NAICS, ISO), supports 40+ P&C and Life & Health business lines, and deploys either standalone or via a flexible API into existing underwriting workbench, CRM, and policy administration systems. Customers include Zurich North America, Guardian, Generali GC&C, Skyward Specialty, AXIS, and Mosaic Insurance, collectively representing roughly $265B in gross written premium. The company raised a $30M Series B in January 2026 and operates from offices in New York City and Lloyd's of London. Sixfold is the named provider behind these capabilities and is distinct from Cytora, a separate UK-based insurance AI provider. The platform is sold as enterprise SaaS to insurance carriers; there is no public self-serve developer portal, public API reference, SDKs, or open-source release — API integration is delivered under enterprise engagement.

providers.name: Dishpatch
providers.description: Dishpatch is a UK-based meal delivery service that partners with renowned chefs and restaurants to deliver restaurant-quality, finish-at-home meals nationwide. Operated by Dishpatch Ltd (part of the Waitrose family), the service curates seasonal menus from chefs such as Michel Roux, Rick Stein, Sabrina Ghayour, Jose Pizarro and Paul Ainsworth. Orders are placed a la carte rather than by subscription, delivered on Fridays in insulated, recyclable packaging via DPD, and arrive pre-prepared for simple finishing steps at home. A paid "Supper Club" membership adds free shipping, exclusive menus, early sale access and spending credits. Dishpatch operates a consumer e-commerce storefront and does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation surface.

providers.name: Kennek
providers.description: Kennek (Kennek Solutions Ltd) is a UK-based fintech providing all-in-one loan management software built for specialist bridge and development lenders. The platform lets lenders originate, manage, and service loans while monitoring funding lines in one place, automating manual workflows, covenant and eligibility calculations, portfolio risk visibility, and investor reporting so lending teams can scale without adding headcount. Founded by former lenders and backed by HV Capital, Kennek is surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a fintech portfolio-company profile; it publishes a marketing site and legal pages but no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: mojiworks
providers.description: Mojiworks is a UK-based social games studio, backed by Balderton Capital, that is pioneering a game genre it calls MuGC (Multi-User Generative Creation) — living, collaborative worlds that communities and AI systems build together. Its released titles include Ready Chef Go, Trivia Party, Chef Showdown and Hatch Cats, and it is building its first MuGC world as a persistent, community-shaped city. The company publishes a public AI Ethics Policy committing to licensed training data, environmental accountability, human oversight and content-safety controls. Mojiworks does not currently expose a public developer platform, API, or SDK; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record and enrichment lead.

providers.name: smol
providers.description: smol (smol.com, formerly reachable via smolproducts.com) is a UK-based Certified B Corporation direct-to-consumer home cleaning brand founded in 2018 by ex-Unilever product leaders. It sells concentrated, eco-conscious laundry capsules, dishwasher tablets, and household cleaning products on a letterbox subscription model designed to cut plastic, carbon, and chemical waste. smol runs a consumer e-commerce storefront and a Zendesk help centre only; enrichment found no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, webhooks, or agent/MCP surface.

providers.name: Wollit
providers.description: Wollit is a UK-based credit-health subscription service (£9.99/month) that helps consumers build and strengthen their credit profile. Authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority for credit-broking activities, Wollit reports rent and subscription payments to Experian, Equifax and TransUnion, and bundles a suite of consumer tools: Rent Reporting, Payment Reporting, an AI credit assistant (Olli), Affordability Boost, Credit Smart lessons, and Credit Wins. It is a consumer-facing fintech app and was surfaced as a portfolio company of Anthemis; it publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Better Origin
providers.description: Better Origin is a UK-based agritech company decarbonizing the food chain by converting food waste into sustainable, locally produced animal feed. Its core technology is a fully automated, AI-controlled containerized insect farm that breeds black soldier fly larvae to consume food waste and produce nutrient-rich insect-based ingredients for pet food, poultry feed, and aquaculture. The systems are remotely monitored and controlled by software and require no specialist knowledge from operators. Better Origin is a portfolio company of Balderton Capital and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Habito
providers.description: Habito is a UK-based digital mortgage broker that lets people research, compare, and apply for mortgages online across the whole of the market, pairing self-serve digital tools with human mortgage experts, alongside related home-buying services. Founded as a fintech in the consumer lending and real-estate space and backed by Ribbit Capital, Habito has since joined Monzo. The company operates a consumer web product (Webflow-hosted marketing site) and does not publish a public developer API program, developer portal, or OpenAPI at the time of this profile; this record is maintained by the API Evangelist network and reflects only publicly verifiable surfaces.

providers.name: Shoobs
providers.description: Shoobs is a UK-based online events discovery and ticketing platform focused on urban culture — Afrobeats, R&B, hip-hop, dancehall, comedy, theatre, festivals, brunches and club nights across London and other British cities. Founded as a Y Combinator-backed startup, Shoobs helps fans find and book tickets to events that match their taste, and lets promoters list and sell tickets for urban and Black-British cultural events. The platform pairs an events listing and discovery site with an integrated editorial blog covering artists, concerts and nightlife. Shoobs is a consumer web product; it does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Taxscouts
providers.description: TaxScouts is a UK online tax-return and Self Assessment service that pairs individuals, sole traders, landlords and investors with accredited accountants to prepare, review and file their taxes with HMRC for a flat fee. Founded in London, TaxScouts was acquired by Taxfix and its taxscouts.com domain now redirects to taxfix.com/en-uk. The service is a consumer-facing web and mobile product with pricing tiers for one-off filing, optimisation with HMRC audit protection, and year-round accountant support. As of this profile it exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API documentation; this record captures its public identity and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Dexory
providers.description: Dexory is a UK-based warehouse intelligence and robotics company whose DexoryView platform pairs fleets of autonomous mobile scanning robots with physical AI to deliver real-time "ground truth" visibility across warehouses and distribution centers. The robots autonomously scan more than 10,000 pallet locations per hour and up to 18 meters of racking height, building a live digital twin that feeds AI-driven analytics for inventory accuracy, space and slotting optimization, damage/compliance detection, and operational performance. DexoryView is organized into modules (Integrity for stock accuracy and automated cycle counts, Optimise for space and productivity analytics, and Adapt for real-time operational response) and connects into existing warehouse and ERP systems such as SAP EWM, Manhattan, Blue Yonder, and Körber through pre-built connectors. Dexory serves 3PL logistics, manufacturing, food & beverage, retail, pharma, and air cargo operators. Added to the API Evangelist network from Atomico's portfolio and enriched via the pipeline; Dexory does not currently publish a public developer portal or OpenAPI.

providers.name: Mindgard
providers.description: Mindgard is a UK-based offensive AI security company (London/Lancaster, spun out of Lancaster University) that provides an automated AI red-teaming and security testing platform for large language models, AI agents, and generative AI systems. Mindgard's platform combines AI Discovery and Recon (mapping the AI attack surface and shadow AI usage), continuous AI Red Teaming against evolving attacker techniques, AI Assessment, AI Runtime Protection, and Model Scanning, backed by a research-led attack library covering jailbreaks (ActorAttack, Crescendo, EvilConfidant, PersonGPT, DevModeV2, AsciiArtAttack, AntiGPT), prompt-injection techniques (Ascii85, AnsiEscaped, AnsiRaw and others), and policy/violation testing (MaliciousGeneration, PromptAlignment). Developers and security teams integrate Mindgard via a public REST API (projects, tests, multi-turn tests, datasets, findings, reconnaissance), a Python CLI (`pip install mindgard`), a Python SDK, a Burp Suite extension, and a GitHub Action for adding red-team checks to MLOps pipelines. The company also maintains and contributes to open-source security tooling including PyRIT integrations, an OpenAI-compatible LLM-Guard proxy, a chatbot API wrapper for testing web chatbots, and proof-of-concept vulnerability demonstrations (document RCE in LangChain agents, hidden audio jailbreaks, prompt-jailbreak demos). Mindgard's commercial model is enterprise SaaS with platform and services tiers; pricing is gated behind a sales conversation, and the platform is positioned for security, AppSec, and AI governance teams testing customer-facing or internally deployed AI systems.

providers.name: Jet2
providers.description: Jet2 plc (London Stock Exchange: JET2, formerly Dart Group plc) is a British leisure travel group headquartered at Low Fare Finder House, Leeds Bradford Airport, Yeadon, Leeds, West Yorkshire — an address confirmed verbatim in the Extended Validation TLS certificate served by www.jet2.com, issued to "JET2.COM LIMITED", company serial number 02739537, jurisdiction GB. Its home market is the United Kingdom. The group combines two businesses that are unusual in this sector for being deliberately fused: Jet2.com (IATA code LS, ICAO code EXS), the UK's third-largest airline, and Jet2holidays, the UK's largest ATOL holder and leading provider of ATOL-protected package holidays to the Mediterranean, the Canary Islands and European city destinations. For the year ended 31 March 2026 the group reported revenue of £7,482.1 million, operating profit of £439.6 million and a record 20.83 million passengers, flying from 14 UK airport bases including newly added London Luton and London Gatwick, with more than 63% of flown passengers buying an end-to-end package holiday and 155 Airbus A321neo aircraft on order. Jet2holidays sells through its own website and through more than 2,500 independent UK travel agent partners, and carries ABTA number Y1256. Where Jet2 sits in the distribution chain is the point of this record. Like easyJet and Ryanair, Jet2.com was built with no Global Distribution System dependency at all: it never filed fares into the GDS rail that Amadeus, Sabre and Travelport have intermediated for forty years, and it therefore never needed IATA's New Distribution Capability as a remedy. Travelport supports Jet2 in Smartpoint only as a "Direct Payment Carrier" — its low-cost-carrier workaround — point-to-point only, no connecting flights, and with no post-booking change or cancellation possible through the GDS at all ("Requests for changes must be made directly through Jet2"). In June 2025 Jet2.com signed a distribution agreement with airline technology company Kyte, whose Kyte Direct Connect (KDC) JSON/REST API "standardises airline NDC and LCC proprietary content", opening Jet2 seats and ancillaries to travel management companies and corporate booking tools for the first time, with the same content reaching agency desktops through AirGateway. Separately, Jet2holidays operates an agency API that lets independent agents sell Jet2 packages on their own bookable websites for commission. Its API posture, stated honestly, is that Jet2 runs real production distribution APIs and publishes nothing about them. There is no developer portal — developer.jet2.com, developers.jet2.com, docs.jet2.com, apis.jet2.com, ndc.jet2.com, partner.jet2.com and trade.jet2.com all fail to resolve — no API reference, no OpenAPI, Swagger, AsyncAPI or GraphQL contract, no security.txt, no .well-known catalogue and no official GitHub organisation. api.jet2.com resolves and answers HTTP 200 with nothing but the stock Microsoft IIS 10.0 default page, 404 on every spec path probed. Access is by commercial agreement only, negotiated bilaterally or through Kyte, whose own FAQ states that "Access to airline products is controlled by each airline." This record is an honest stub: apis[] is intentionally empty because no Jet2 API is publicly documented, and listing an undocumented hostname as an API would be fabrication. The evidence, including every URL probed with its HTTP status, is in review.yml. A second enrichment pass on 28 July 2026 found the one genuinely public first-party developer surface Jet2 has, and it is not an API: the Jet2 Design System, published as two npm packages under the @jet2 scope (design tokens for seven brand themes, and a React component library containing a single Button), sourced from Jet2's private Azure DevOps organisation at jet2tfs.visualstudio.com/Jet2Digital and documented at design.jet2.com behind a Supernova login. Both packages were last published in April 2024. The same pass confirmed no /.well-known/ document on any host that answers, no security.txt, no vulnerability disclosure programme, no trust centre, no public Postman collection and no SDK in any package registry. Jet2's engineering voice, such as it is, comes from Jet2 Travel Technologies (J2TT), its in-house development centre in Pune, India, which runs a public blog with an RSS feed.

providers.name: Sourceful
providers.description: Sourceful is a Manchester, United Kingdom packaging technology company that began as a sustainable packaging marketplace connecting brands with vetted manufacturers and offering data-driven carbon footprint, life-cycle, and recyclability metrics for every packaging design. Founded in 2020 by Wing Chan and Charlie Bradshaw, the company raised roughly $32M from investors including Index Ventures, Coatue, and Eka Ventures, and grew to over 100 employees serving climate-conscious consumer brands. Since 2024–2025 Sourceful has pivoted toward AI-powered visual design for packaging, releasing Sourceful 3.0 and Riverflow 1, a proprietary image-editing foundation model marketed as state-of-the-art for design-grade, print-ready packaging artwork. The current product line covers AI logo design, packaging design, AI product photography, image editing, packaging ranges, flavor/variant ranges, brand moodboards, and (announced) product mockups and social ads. Sourceful is ISO 42001 certified for AI management. As of this profile the company does not publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or open-source GitHub organization for the packaging/design platform, and the original sustainable-packaging marketplace surface and supplier-facing carbon footprint API have been superseded by the AI design product; there is no Sourceful developer portal at this time. The unrelated github.com/sourceful organization belongs to Pony Foo, not this company, and sourceful.energy is a separate distributed-energy-resource platform unrelated to Sourceful Ltd.

providers.name: Alchemab Therapeutics
providers.description: Alchemab Therapeutics is a UK-based clinical-stage biotechnology company developing next-generation antibody therapeutics for hard-to-treat diseases. Its "Adaptive Immunity" platform identifies naturally resilient individuals, such as long-term cancer survivors, and harnesses their protective antibodies, using artificial intelligence and deep learning to translate these natural immune responses into novel human-derived therapeutics across neurodegeneration, oncology, and other areas of high unmet need. Alchemab was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. As a research-stage therapeutics company it publishes no public developer API program, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications at this time.

providers.name: IONA
providers.description: IONA (IONA Drones) is a UK-based autonomous drone delivery company building the full technology stack for logistics operators. Its tilt-rotor Sonnet aircraft performs VTOL from compact sites and carries up to 20 parcels up to 200 km per autonomous flight. IONA pairs the aircraft with an onboard autonomy operating system, GPS/LiDAR sensor-fusion precision landing, a SORA-aligned BVLOS compliance engine, an operations centre for real-time fleet monitoring and analytics, and a digital twin for simulation and predictive maintenance. The platform integrates with existing TMS/WMS logistics systems and targets healthcare, rural/remote, express e-commerce, industrial, and maritime delivery. Backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Material Evolution
providers.description: Material Evolution is a UK-based cleantech manufacturer of ultra-low carbon cement for the construction industry. Its MevoCem and MevoXL products use a proprietary "Alkali Fusion" process to transform industrial byproducts into cement feedstocks, achieving a 52.5N strength rating at roughly 144-196 kg CO2e per tonne versus ordinary Portland cement. The company operates compact, automated factories (including its Wrexham facility) and applies AI to material development and feedstock optimization. It is a B2B cement supplier and does not currently publish any public developer-facing API, developer portal, or technical documentation surface.

providers.name: NOTHS
providers.description: NOTHS (Not On The High Street, notonthehighstreet.com) is a UK online marketplace that curates and sells unique gifts, jewellery, homeware and personalised products made or sourced by thousands of small UK creative businesses. Founded in 2006 and backed by Index Ventures, the platform connects independent sellers ("partners") with consumers through a curated storefront, seller onboarding, and an affiliate programme. It exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface; its api.notonthehighstreet.com host is a private backend serving the company's own web and mobile storefront. This profile is a VC-portfolio lead enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline via live domain/security probing.

providers.name: THG
providers.description: THG plc (formerly The Hut Group) is a UK-based consumer brands group founded in 2004 in Manchester and listed on the London Stock Exchange. Following the 2025 demerger of its Ingenuity technology and fulfilment division, THG is a pure-play consumer brands business operating two divisions: THG Beauty (home to Lookfantastic, Cult Beauty, Dermstore and prestige brand partners) and THG Nutrition (led by Myprotein, one of the world's largest online sports-nutrition brands). THG designs, manufactures and sells beauty and nutrition products direct-to-consumer across global markets. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Balderton Capital, an early investor. THG operates corporate, investor-relations and careers web properties but publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; this profile captures its identity and a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Gyre Energy
providers.description: Gyre Energy is a UK-based climate-tech company that reduces cooling costs for operators of cold storage facilities, data centers, and building portfolios by combining artificial intelligence with thermal energy storage. Its platform pairs Gyre AI, a digital twin that learns a facility's thermal behavior and shifts cooling cycles to run when grid energy is cheapest and greenest, with an integrated thermal energy storage "cold battery" and a real-time monitoring and controls layer that tracks temperature, energy use, and door-open events. The company reports up to 50% lower cooling expenses, 38% verified energy cost savings at its first commercial cold storage deployment, a 91% reduction in temperature excursions, and a payback period of under 1.5 years. Gyre Energy is a portfolio company of Speedinvest and, as of July 2026, secured $1.3m in funding to support a major blue-chip deployment and global scaling. It currently exposes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal; this profile captures its identity and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Vsim
providers.description: Vsim (Vsim Technology Ltd) is a Manchester, UK physics-simulation startup founded in 2022 by ex-NVIDIA simulation engineers Michelle Lu (CEO) and Kier Storey (CTO). The company builds a next-generation physics simulation platform and an end-to-end reinforcement-learning training framework for robotics, reporting up to 100x training performance speed-ups over existing solutions, with applications across robotics, AI, visual effects, aerodynamics, gaming, and e-commerce. Vsim raised a $21.5M seed round led by EQT Ventures (total ~$24M). It does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: lovecrafts
providers.description: LoveCrafts (LoveCrafts Group Limited) is a UK-based crafting commerce and community platform — "your home to shop, share and dream in crafts" — selling yarns and fibers, knitting, crochet, sewing, quilting and embroidery patterns, supplies, tools, kits and fabrics, alongside free and paid patterns, tutorials and inspiration content. It operates localized storefronts for North America, the UK, Germany, Australia and France on a Nuxt-based e-commerce stack. LoveCrafts was surfaced as a portfolio company of Balderton Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. It exposes no public developer portal or API surface; the only machine-discoverable public artifact is an RFC 9116 security.txt with a responsible- disclosure policy (no bug bounty programme).

providers.name: EXMO
providers.description: Cryptocurrencies exchange based in UK

providers.name: Hawk-Eye Innovations
providers.description: Hawk-Eye Innovations is a Basingstoke, UK-headquartered sports technology company and part of the Sony Group, specializing in precision optical tracking, electronic officiating, video replay, and performance analytics across 25+ professional sports in 100+ countries. Founded in 2001 by Paul Hawkins and acquired by Sony in 2011, Hawk-Eye operates alongside Pulselive and Beyond Sports within Sony's sports division. The company is the standard for ball-tracking in tennis (Electronic Line Calling, now used in place of human line judges at the major tours), goal-line technology and semi-automated offside in football (Premier League, FIFA), video replay in cricket (DRS), NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, rugby, and PGA Tour shot-tracking. Core product platforms include SMART Replay, SMART Track, SMART Insight, HawkAR, iHawk, HawkREPLAY, HawkNEST, HawkVISION, SkeleTRACK, Electronic Line Calling, Goal Line Technology, Semi-Automated Offside Technology, and VAR systems. Revenue comes from long-term contracts with leagues, federations, and broadcasters; there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for Hawk-Eye products. All integrations are bespoke and delivered through Sony Sports Business / Hawk-Eye operations teams.

providers.name: Tuza
providers.description: Tuza is a banking automation platform that orchestrates AI agents, customers and workflows to eliminate the manual processes that slow banks down. Originally launched in the UK at tuza.co.uk as a card-payment fee comparison and switching service for merchants, the company has repositioned as Tuza AI, delivering agentic automation for banks. It is an early-stage, venture-backed fintech (backed by Northzone) building a product that connects AI agents with core banking operations and customer-facing workflows. As of this profile Tuza publishes a marketing and careers site only — no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation surface has been released yet, so this record captures verified company identity plus a domain-security probe.

providers.name: Ubiquisys
providers.description: Ubiquisys was a UK-based developer of intelligent 3G/LTE/Wi-Fi small cells and femtocells for mobile operators, with products like ActiveRadio, ActiveSON, CloudBase, and EdgeCloud deployed by carriers such as SFR and SoftBank, and was ranked #1 in ABI Research's Small Cell Vendor Matrix. Backed by Accel, Cisco announced its intent to acquire Ubiquisys on April 3, 2013, and the company was absorbed into Cisco's small cell portfolio; ubiquisys.com is now Cisco-owned and redirects to Cisco's acquisitions page. Ubiquisys published no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Exscientia
providers.description: Exscientia was an Oxford UK-based AI-driven precision medicine and drug design company, founded in 2012 as a spin-out from the University of Dundee. Its platform combined generative chemistry (Centaur Chemist) with patient tissue-based screening (EVE, an automated single-cell platform for testing drug candidates directly against patient-derived tumor samples) to design small-molecule drug candidates faster and at lower cost than conventional pharma R&D. Notable firsts included EXS-21546 (an A2A antagonist developed with Evotec), DSP-1181 (the first AI-designed molecule to enter human clinical trials, with Sumitomo Dainippon Pharma), and DSP-0038 (a dual 5-HT1A/5-HT2A modulator for Alzheimer's psychosis). Exscientia maintained active pharma partnerships with Sanofi, Bristol Myers Squibb, Bayer, Sumitomo, and Merck KGaA. Exscientia was acquired by Recursion Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ: RXRX) in an all-stock deal that closed in November 2024; the combined company operates under the Recursion brand and the legacy exscientia.ai website now redirects to recursion.com. The Exscientia name persists primarily through its GitHub organization, which continues to host open-source scientific Python packages for molecular predictive modelling (molflux), physics-based ML potentials (physicsml), antibody structure prediction (abodybuilder3), and biomolecular simulation (biosimspace) used by the wider computational chemistry and structural biology community. Exscientia did not expose any public commercial APIs, SDKs, or developer products before or after the merger; platform access was always delivered through collaborative drug-discovery agreements.

providers.name: Twinn Health
providers.description: Twinn Health builds preventive whole-body MRI infrastructure for early disease detection, pairing AI-structured imaging reports and longitudinal health data pipelines with imaging providers and wellness clinics in the UK, Saudi Arabia, and the wider Middle East. Founded at Imperial College London, validated with UK-based NHS clinicians, and backed by 500 Global and Wa'ed Ventures, it also offers expert MRI report interpretation for individuals. Twinn Health publishes no public API or developer surface as of July 2026.

providers.name: Trussle
providers.description: Trussle was a UK online mortgage broker founded in 2015 and backed by Seedcamp, offering a consumer-facing mortgage comparison, application and monitoring service. It was acquired and rebranded as Better.co.uk (trading as Trussle Lab Ltd, authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority); the trussle.com domain now 301-redirects entirely to better.co.uk. As of this enrichment pass Trussle publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or API documentation.

providers.name: Getagent
providers.description: GetAgent is a UK PropTech company operating getagent.co.uk, a consumer-facing service that helps home sellers compare and choose estate agents based on independent performance data such as sold prices, time-to-sell, and fees. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Seedcamp, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment. No public developer portal, API, or specification surface was discoverable at the time of this pass; the production site is served behind a bot-protection checkpoint, so this profile currently carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: getdinghy
providers.description: Dinghy (getdinghy.com) was a UK insurtech offering on-demand professional indemnity and business insurance for freelancers and contractors, and a Balderton Capital portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the domain no longer serves an independent site - its TLS certificate and HTTP responses resolve to Kingsbridge Group infrastructure (kingsbridge.co.uk / kingsbridgegroup.com / kng.io) and every path returns HTTP 502, indicating the brand has been absorbed by Kingsbridge. No public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or well-known discovery surface is exposed, so no spec-grounded artifacts could be searched or derived. Retained as a network lead with evidence of the successor.

providers.name: Circle Health Group
providers.description: Circle Health Group is the largest independent operator of private hospitals in the United Kingdom, running a nationwide network of hospitals and clinics that provide diagnostics, surgery, physiotherapy, and consultant-led private medical care to self-pay patients, insured patients, and the NHS. Originally backed by Balderton Capital as Circle Holdings, the group offers services spanning orthopaedics, cardiology, gynaecology, general surgery, and imaging. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; the organization operates a consumer-facing patient website and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal surface.

providers.name: PCV
providers.description: Precision Cardiovascular (PCV) is a UK-based digital-health company advancing cardiovascular care through continuous, AI-powered heart-failure monitoring. Its flagship PULSENSE system pairs an implantable pulmonary-artery-pressure (PAP) sensor insert and a wearable smart chest patch with an AI-powered clinical app that surfaces real-time pressure trends and analytics for clinicians and patients. The platform is designed to catch PAP fluctuations that traditional spot-check measurements miss, including overnight and during activity. PCV PULSENSE is an investigational device under regulatory review (FDA, MHRA, EMA) and is not yet approved for commercial sale. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and profiled in the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: Signify Group
providers.description: Signify Group is a London, United Kingdom-based ethical data science firm founded in 2017 by co-founder and CEO Jonathan Hirshler, applying machine learning, natural language understanding, and open-source intelligence (OSINT) to social and digital media data. Its flagship service, Threat Matrix, is widely regarded as the leading platform for detecting, analysing, evidencing, and actioning online abuse and fixated threats directed at athletes, clubs, leagues, player unions, federations, brands, and other public figures. Threat Matrix scans incoming public messages across X (Twitter), Instagram, Facebook, and TikTok in 39+ languages, uses "augmented intelligence" (AI speed combined with trained human analyst nuance) to triage racist, sexist, homophobic, anti-semitic, islamophobic, gambling-driven, and personally targeted abuse, and produces evidence-grade reports with network mapping that can be used by platforms, police, sponsors, and protection teams. Customers and partners include the Professional Footballers' Association (PFA), Kick It Out, the International Tennis Federation (ITF) and WTA Tour covering c.8,300 players, the International Ski and Snowboard Federation (FIS) protecting 1,000+ athletes and officials, the Badminton World Federation (BWF), the NCAA, and Japan's 2026 World Baseball Classic squad. Signify also operates ShareScore (media coverage and social buzz analytics), Sports Insights (fan engagement and athlete insight analytics), and Online Forensics (brand reputation, OSINT investigations, and risk assurance). Signify is a private services firm with no public developer API, no public SDKs, and no public GitHub organization; engagement is via direct sales and managed service contracts with rights-holders, leagues, federations, and enterprise clients.

providers.name: Tekever
providers.description: Tekever is a multinational defence technology company headquartered in Lisbon, Portugal, with operations in the United Kingdom (Bath and a planned large-scale drone production facility in Swindon), France (Toulouse and Cahors), and the United States (Fayetteville, North Carolina). Founded in 2001, the company specialises in AI-driven autonomy for civil and defence missions, with its core business centred on long-endurance Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) used for Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR), maritime surveillance, and electronic warfare. Its flagship platforms include the AR3, a configurable medium-range tactical UAS (designated StormShroud in service with the UK Royal Air Force), the AR5, a SATCOM-enabled long-endurance maritime and land ISR aircraft, and the ARX, a next-generation system positioned as the company's game changer. These platforms are paired with ATLAS, Tekever's real-time intelligence-as-a-service platform that fuses sensor and satellite data into actionable mission intelligence. Tekever drones are operated by the UK Ministry of Defence, the British Army, the Armed Forces of Ukraine (with the UK having committed approximately £270 million in Tekever UAVs for Ukraine since the start of the Russian invasion), the European Maritime Safety Agency under a €30 million contract, the French Ministry of Armed Forces (CNES/DGA), Portugal, and NATO. The company also develops satellite technology and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) capabilities to extend its intelligence services beyond the airborne domain. Tekever's revenue model is built on government and defence contracts, platform sales, and managed ISR-as-a-service offerings; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source release, and engagement with the company is conducted through direct sales, government procurement, and partnership channels.

providers.name: Cambridge Aerospace
providers.description: Cambridge Aerospace is a UK-based defense technology company, incorporated in September 2024, developing scalable interceptor missiles and sovereign air-and-missile-defense systems for European nations. Its first product, Skyhammer, is a tube-launched subsonic interceptor with a Cambridge-developed radar seeker, positioned as an affordable, mass-producible counter to drones and cruise missiles (often likened to an Iron Dome-style layered air defense). The company operates in the aerospace and defense/security sector and is backed by a venture syndicate including Accel, Lakestar, Lux Capital, Spark Capital, and the D3 fund. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel; it is a hardware-first defense company with no public API or developer surface at this time.

providers.name: Cazoo
providers.description: Cazoo was a UK online used-car retailer founded in 2018 by Alex Chesterman, offering a direct-to-consumer platform to buy, sell, and finance used cars fully online with home delivery. The company listed on the New York Stock Exchange via a SPAC merger in 2021 before restructuring and entering administration in 2024; its consumer marketplace brand was subsequently sold. Cazoo was surfaced as a portfolio company of D1 Capital, General Catalyst, and Sapphire Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. No public developer portal or API surface was found during enrichment: the site is behind bot protection (HTTP 429) and no /.well-known/ discovery documents are published. Sector: ecommerce / automotive retail.

providers.name: CleanCo
providers.description: CleanCo is a United Kingdom-based beverage company, founded in 2019 by Spencer Matthews, that produces premium low- and no-alcohol alternative spirits. Its product line replicates the flavour profiles of traditional spirits across key categories, including CleanGin, CleanRum, CleanVodka and CleanTequila, aimed at consumers who want to reduce alcohol consumption without sacrificing taste. The company sells direct-to-consumer through cleanliquor.com and through grocery and hospitality retail channels across the UK and international markets. CleanCo raised venture funding from Lightspeed Venture Partners in 2020. It is a consumer packaged-goods brand and does not publish a developer API, developer portal, or any machine-readable API surface; it is retained in the API Evangelist network only as an identified Lightspeed portfolio company, not as an API provider.

providers.name: crowdcube
providers.description: Crowdcube is a UK-based equity crowdfunding platform that lets everyday and professional investors buy shares in early-stage and growth-stage private companies, and lets founders raise capital directly from their community and the wider crowd. Founded in 2011 in Exeter by Darren Westlake and Luke Lang, it is authorised and regulated by the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) and has helped hundreds of startups and scale-ups raise funding from a large base of retail investors. The platform covers pitch discovery, investment processing, share issuance, nominee shareholding, and a secondary-market cashout facility. Crowdcube surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Balderton Capital. It does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; this profile captures its company identity and observable domain-security posture.

providers.name: Dealflo
providers.description: Dealflo was a UK-based financial-technology company that provided an automated agreement, identity-verification, and e-signature platform used by lenders and financial institutions to capture, verify, and legally bind financial agreements end to end. It was acquired by OneSpan (formerly VASCO Data Security) in September 2018 for roughly USD 55 million and folded into OneSpan's Digital Agreements / electronic-signature product line. The dealflo.com domain now 301-redirects to onespan.com and Dealflo no longer operates an independent developer program, public documentation, or API. This record is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio/company lead surfaced from the HV Capital portfolio; no independent API artifacts exist to enrich because the product surface has been absorbed by OneSpan.

providers.name: Fluidly
providers.description: Fluidly was a London-based intelligent cashflow forecasting fintech founded in 2016 by Caroline Plumb, providing SME cash-flow prediction, scenario planning, and working-capital tools used by roughly 1,300 UK accountancy firms. OakNorth Bank acquired Fluidly in December 2021 and folded the product into its Credit Intelligence Suite; the independent Fluidly brand has since been retired and fluidly.com now redirects to OakNorth's partnerships page. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as an acquired-company record — no independent Fluidly developer portal, OpenAPI, or public API surface remains.

providers.name: Givemetap
providers.description: GiveMeTap is a UK-based social-enterprise consumer brand that designs and sells reusable, BPA-free stainless-steel and insulated water bottles (500ml and 700ml, plus custom co-branded bottles for businesses). For every bottle sold, GiveMeTap funds five years of clean drinking water for a person in Ghana, giving 20% of its revenue to water projects in Africa; the company reports 116,391 people reached with clean water for life. It operates a direct-to-consumer e-commerce storefront on the Shopify platform. GiveMeTap is a physical-products company with no first-party developer API, developer portal, or public API documentation; it was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio lead and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub.

providers.name: Hassle
providers.description: Hassle.com was a London-based on-demand home-cleaning marketplace, founded in 2012 by Alex Depledge and Jules Coleman, connecting households with vetted local cleaners for one-off and recurring bookings. Backed by Accel Partners, it was acquired by Rocket Internet-backed Helpling in July 2015 for a reported EUR 32 million to form one of the world's largest home-cleaning marketplaces. The Hassle.com brand was subsequently folded into Helpling, whose UK operations have since ceased; the domain now redirects to Helpling. The company operates a consumer-facing web/mobile booking product and exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: nested
providers.description: Nested is a modern, technology-enabled UK estate agency that helps people sell, buy, and let residential property. It pairs hyper-local human agents with a digital platform and mobile app that give sellers transparency across the transaction, listing homes on major portals such as Rightmove, Zoopla, and OnTheMarket. Nested was surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and northzone and added to the API Evangelist network. The company operates a consumer-facing service and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or technical documentation at this time.

providers.name: Newmark Group
providers.description: Newmark Group, Inc. (NASDAQ: NMRK) is a global commercial real estate advisory and services firm headquartered in New York City. Founded in 1929 and acquired by BGC Partners in October 2011, Newmark provides capital markets, leasing, valuation & advisory, global corporate services (GCS), property management, industrial and logistics, multifamily, and retail services. The firm expanded its international footprint with the 2023 acquisition of UK-based Gerald Eve and its multifamily platform via Open Realty Advisors. Newmark publishes recurring industry research under the MarketBeat / market-report brand but does not operate a public developer program or expose machine-readable APIs.

providers.name: OneSwoop
providers.description: OneSwoop is a UK car-buying and new-car price-comparison website, founded in 1999 and based in Liverpool, England, that lets consumers compare prices on brand-new cars and buy them online at a discount. It operates as a consumer-facing e-commerce and comparison property and publishes no public developer platform, API, documentation, or SDK surface. Backed historically by Insight Partners and other venture investors, it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile rather than an API provider.

providers.name: PrimaryBid
providers.description: PrimaryBid was a UK-based fintech that gave retail investors access to public capital markets — IPOs, follow-on equity raises, and public offerings that were historically restricted to institutional investors. It partnered with exchanges, banks, and issuers to broadcast live capital-raising events to individual investors, powering retail participation in listings such as Deliveroo, PensionBee, and Soho House. PrimaryBid's technology was acquired by SoFi Technologies, Inc. in May 2026; the standalone consumer platform has been wound down and its public website now redirects former shareholders to third-party share registrars. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record. No public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Quantum Motion
providers.description: Quantum Motion is a UK-based full-stack quantum computing company building scalable, fault-tolerant quantum computers using silicon (CMOS) technology, the same manufacturing process used for conventional microchips. Spun out of University College London and the University of Oxford, the company develops qubit control hardware, cryogenic electronics, and quantum architecture aimed at manufacturing quantum processors at scale. It is a research- and hardware-focused company rather than an API or developer-platform provider; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDK surface could be verified (the corporate site sits behind bot-challenge protection and web search was unavailable), so the profile remains identity-only.

providers.name: rentify
providers.description: Rentify was a London-based property technology (PropTech) startup founded in 2011 that built an online lettings and property-management platform for landlords, letting them list, market, price, and manage rental properties directly without a traditional high-street agent. It raised a Series A from Balderton Capital and later a crowdfunding round before ceasing operations. Surfaced as a balderton-capital portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the enrichment pass found no live developer portal, documentation, or public API surface (the company is no longer operating and rentify.com no longer serves an application).

providers.name: SimplyCook
providers.description: SimplyCook is a UK-based recipe-box and meal-flavoring subscription service (tagline "For simple pleasures, SimplyCook.") that ships monthly boxes of flavor pots, stocks, and spice blends alongside curated recipes so subscribers can cook varied meals at home in around twenty minutes. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. SimplyCook operates as a direct-to-consumer e-commerce brand; it runs an internal application backend at api.simplycook.com but publishes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface. This profile therefore carries only what could be genuinely probed: DNS/TLS/HTTP domain-security posture for the company domain.

providers.name: taptrip.co
providers.description: TapTrip (taptrip.co) was a UK-based self-serve business travel and expense booking platform for SMEs, founded in 2018 in Manchester and part of the Barclays Accelerator powered by Techstars. It let smaller businesses book and manage flights, hotels, rail, and ground transportation without a travel management company. TapTrip was acquired by TripStax in July 2022 and folded into the TripStax platform as an SME online-booking module for travel management companies; the standalone brand was absorbed. As of this enrichment pass the taptrip.co domain no longer hosts an active product — it resolves to a ParkingCrew domain-parking service and the TLS endpoint does not respond. No public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface was found for the standalone company.

providers.name: thetab
providers.description: The Tab (thetab.com) is a UK-based digital media and entertainment publication operated by Digitalbox Publishing Ltd (Co Reg No. 09909897). It covers celebrity and reality-TV news, viral trends, gaming, politics, and university and campus culture across a network of youth-focused verticals, monetized primarily through advertising (advertise.thetab.com). Surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and added to the API Evangelist network. As of the 2026-07-21 enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, /.well-known/ discovery surface, or llms.txt (all probed and returned HTTP 404); this remains an editorial/advertising media property with no developer-facing product.

providers.name: Thread
providers.description: Thread (thread.com) was a UK-based fashion technology company that combined AI with human expert stylists to deliver personalized clothing recommendations for men and women. Founded by Kieran O'Neill and Ben Phillips and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Balderton Capital, Thread's brand, technology and data were acquired by Marks & Spencer. The company subsequently entered administration and has ceased trading; its site now serves only a shutdown notice. Enrichment found no public API, developer portal, documentation, or event surface. This profile is retained as a network record of a defunct portfolio company.

providers.name: Vinterior
providers.description: Vinterior is a UK-based curated online marketplace for vintage, antique, and pre-owned furniture and homeware. It connects independent sellers, dealers, and restorers with buyers looking for one-of-a-kind pieces, positioning itself as a more sustainable alternative to mass-produced furniture. The platform handles product discovery, listings, seller storefronts, checkout, and delivery for design-led vintage goods. Vinterior is backed by Seedcamp. As of this profile Vinterior does not publish a public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API surface; this record is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company profile and enrichment lead.

providers.name: City Reach International
providers.description: City Reach International Limited was a UK-registered telecommunications and internet-infrastructure company, incorporated 14 April 2000 at 8 Salisbury Square, Blackfriars, London EC4Y 8BB (Companies House number 03973748), classified under SIC 6420 (telecommunications) and 7260 (other computer related activities). It was a dot-com era venture backed in part by Battery Ventures, and appears on the Battery Ventures all-companies list, which is how it entered the API Evangelist network. The company was dissolved on 13 May 2014. Enrichment probing in July 2026 found no surviving corporate website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface: the candidate domains cityreach.com, cityreachinternational.com, cityreach.net and cityreachinternational.co.uk do not resolve, and cityreach.co.uk resolves only to a parked domain-for-sale landing page. There is no API, specification, SDK, or event surface to catalog for this company, and none should be fabricated.

providers.name: Lanistar
providers.description: Lanistar was a London-based consumer fintech founded in 2019 by Gurhan Kiziloz, known for a heavily influencer-marketed "polymorphic" Mastercard debit card with an on-card keypad and display that generated single-use PIN and CVV2 codes. Lanistar Limited operated as an EMD agent of Modulr FS Limited under FCA authorisation, with cards issued by AF Payments Limited, and pivoted its consumer launch to Brazil where it offered a mobile account, Pix transfers and in-app crypto buying and selling. The company never operated a developer program: no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, SDK, or public GitHub repository was ever published. Lanistar Limited (company number 12091938) was placed into compulsory liquidation by a court winding-up order filed 14 April 2025, and its public surface has since gone dark — lanistar.com and lanistar.app no longer resolve to any web host, the lanistar.co.uk domain is listed for sale by a domain broker, and the com.lanistar Google Play listing has been removed. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

bands.label: Not Yet Rated
bands.blurb: Providers we have not scored yet — unknown, not zero.

providers.name: Anthemis Group
providers.description: Anthemis Group is a London-based venture capital and asset management firm founded in 2010 by Amy Nauiokas (Group CEO) and Sean Park (Group CIO), both former capital-markets executives. Anthemis invests to "architect the digital economy," concentrating on financial technology and its adjacencies: embedded finance, payments and banking infrastructure, insurtech, wealthtech, crypto and digital assets, climate and agtech finance, and applied AI for financial services. The firm invests primarily at pre-seed, seed, Series A and early Series B, writing checks generally in the ~$2M-$3M range, and pairs venture investing with an advisory and platform practice aimed at systematically transforming financial services. Anthemis is headquartered in London with additional presence in New York, Geneva, Amsterdam, Lisbon and Dallas, manages roughly $500M in assets, and has backed 300+ companies including Betterment, eToro, Carta, Pipe, TrueLayer, Tide, Currencycloud, Atom Bank and The Climate Corporation.
